q: According to Pound, law is:
o: The statement of circumstances in which the public force will be brought to bear upon men through courts
A social institution to satisfy social wants
Aggregate of rules set by men as politically superior or sovereign, to men as politically subject
A crystallized common sense of communities
e: Roscoe Pound saw law as a social institution that satisfies social wants by securing as many interests as possible with the least friction (law as social engineering).

q: Which of the following is not correct in relation to rights in its various forms and its correlatives?
e: In Hohfeld's scheme the correlative of Power is Liability, not Liberty.

q: The main purpose of corporation sole is:
o: To protect the property of the Government
To make the property easily transferable
To make the property easily inheritable
To make continuity of an office
e: A corporation sole is a single incumbent (e.g. the President or a Bishop) treated as a legal person so that the office continues unbroken despite changes in the holder.

q: "Every man has a property in his own person, he has right to preserve his property, that is, his life, liberty and estate" - is said by:
e: This is John Locke's natural-rights theory of property: life, liberty and estate are held as property in one's own person.

q:
Under the special powers of Rajya Sabha which of the following resolutions can originate only in Rajya Sabha?
(A) Resolution seeking removal of Vice President
(B) Any resolution seeking creation of one or more all India service
(C) Any resolution seeking legislation on state subject
(D) Introduction of money bills
e: Art. 67(b) (removal of Vice-President), Art. 312 (all-India services) and Art. 249 (legislation on a State List subject) resolutions are moved in the Rajya Sabha. Money bills originate only in the Lok Sabha.

q: Vice President of India on expiry of his term:
o: Gets a mandatory extension of 2 months
Continues to hold office until successor enters upon office
Elects his successor before relinquishing office
e: Under Art. 67(c) the Vice-President continues in office until his successor enters upon office, even after the term expires.

q: State Emergency or President Rule under Article 356 can be imposed in a State by the President for a maximum period of:
e: Proclamation under Art. 356 lasts 6 months initially and can be extended in stages, but never beyond a maximum of 3 years.

q: Besides providing for a functional government and consequential growth in the administrative process, the Constitution has provided elaborate control mechanism so that water may not over-run beyond banks. This has been ensured in which of the following articles of the Constitution?
e: Judicial control over administrative action comes through writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Art. 32), High Courts (Art. 226) and High Courts' supervisory power (Art. 227).

q: Which of the following groups of Jurists who consider the law as a command of sovereign enforced by a superior political authority and accordingly subscribe to the view that International Law is not law as 'properly so called'?
e: Hobbes, Pufendorf and Austin hold the command theory; as international law lacks a sovereign commander, Austin called it only 'positive international morality'.

q: Which one of the following Geneva conventions has the provisions on, "The protection of the victims of maritime warfare"?
e: The Second Geneva Convention covers wounded, sick and shipwrecked members of armed forces at sea. The First covers land forces, the Third prisoners of war, the Fourth civilians.

q: The World Court refused to give its Advisory opinion in which of the following case?
o: The legality of the use by a State of Nuclear weapons in Armed conflict
Legality of the Threat or use of Nuclear weapons case
e: In 1996 the ICJ declined the WHO's request on legality of use of nuclear weapons by a State in armed conflict, as the question was outside WHO's scope. It did answer the General Assembly's request (option D).

q: Which of the following is not the principal organ of the United Nations?
e: The six principal organs are the General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ and Secretariat. There is no 'International Human Rights Commission' among them.

q: The distinctive features of 'Rioting' are an activity which is accompanied by:
e: Rioting (Sec. 146 IPC) is the use of force or violence by an unlawful assembly, or any member of it, in prosecution of its common object. Use of force and violence is its distinguishing feature.

q: Which among the following is the most serious offence, and thus severely punishable?
e: Rioting (Sec. 147 IPC) carries up to 2 years, higher than unlawful assembly (6 months, Sec. 143), affray (1 month, Sec. 160) or simple assault (3 months, Sec. 352).

q: 'Stalking' (following a woman despite her disinterest, spying, etc) is an offence under:
e: Stalking was inserted as Sec. 354D IPC by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013. 354A is sexual harassment and 354B is assault with intent to disrobe.

q: In which of the following cases the supreme court observed, "There is a thin line between the preparation for and an attempt to commit an offence"?
o: State of Maharashtra V Mohd. Yakub
Abhayanand Mishra V. State of Bihar
Malkiat Singh V. State of Punjab
Om Parkesh V. State of Punjab
e: Abhayanand Mishra v. State of Bihar (1961) is the case on the thin line between preparation and attempt to commit an offence.

q: Motor vehicle Amendment Act of 2019 refer to the earlier Motor vehicle Act of 1988 as:
e: An amending Act refers to the Act it amends as the 'Principal Act'.

q: "The courts have created new torts by the gradual and sometimes almost imperceptible extension of old tort", who said the above statement?
e: As per the published answer key, this observation on courts extending old torts into new ones is attributed to Professor Goodhart.

q: Mental condition of a wrong doer at the time of wrong doing is:
o: Relevant in torts based on fault
Relevant in tort based on strict liability
e: Intention, malice or negligence matter where liability depends on fault. In strict or absolute liability the defendant's state of mind is irrelevant.

q: Section 53 of Consumer Protection Act of 2019 provides for establishment of National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. It is to be known as:
e: Sec. 53 provides that the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission shall be known as the 'National Commission'.

q: In a contract of Guarantee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 there are:
e: A guarantee involves creditor, principal debtor and surety, with three contracts: principal debtor-creditor, creditor-surety, and an implied one between surety and principal debtor.

q: In case of unascertained goods, the property in goods passes:
o: When the parties intend the property in goods to pass
As soon as the contract of sale is signed
After the payment of goods is received by the seller
e: Under Sec. 18 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, no property passes in unascertained goods until they are ascertained.

q: Where the money received from a third party by the firm, in ordinary course of business, is misapplied by one of the partners to his own use, then:
o: Defaulting partner alone is liable for the same
Firm is liable for the same
Firm is not liable for the same
e: Sec. 27 of the Indian Partnership Act makes the firm liable to make good the loss where a partner misapplies money received by the firm in the ordinary course of business.

q: Who among the following can remove the name of company from Register of Companies on suo moto basis in terms of Section 248(1) of Companies Act, 2013?
o: Securities and exchange Board of India
e: Sec. 248(1) empowers the Registrar of Companies to remove the name of a defunct company from the register after following the prescribed notice procedure.

q: Which one of the following is 'NOT' a primary source of Muslim Law?
e: Primary sources are the Quran, Sunnat, Ijma and Qiyas. Urf (custom) is a secondary source.

q: Originally under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, divorce was based on:
e: The 1955 Act allowed divorce only on proof of a matrimonial offence (fault) such as adultery or cruelty. Consent (Sec. 13B) and some breakdown grounds were added later.

q: Which of the following judgment does not deal with the need of enactment of 'Uniform Civil Code' in India?
o: Mohd. Ahmad Khan V. Shah Bano Begum
Sarla Mudgal V. Union of India
John Vallamatton V. Union of India
e: Ashok Hurra v. Rupa Bipin Zaveri (2002) dealt with curative petitions. The other three cases all urged a Uniform Civil Code.

q: Which of the following judgment do not deal with the matter of Live-in relationship?
e: Sharda v. Dharmpal (2003) concerned medical examination of a spouse in matrimonial proceedings and the right to privacy, not live-in relationships.

q: The Supreme Court of India recognised the significance of Inter-generational equity and held a government department's approval to establish forest based Industry to be invalid in one of the following case:
o: State of Himachal Pradesh V. Ganesh Wood products
Vellore citizen's forum V. Union of India
Dr. B.L. Wadehra V Union of India
M.C. Metha V Union of India
e: In State of H.P. v. Ganesh Wood Products (1995) the Court quashed approval for a forest-based industry, stressing inter-generational equity and sustainable development.

q: The preamble to both Environment (Protection) Act and Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act were passed to implement the decision reached in one of the following:
o: United Nations Conference on Environment and Development, 1992
United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, 1972
e: Both Acts refer to the 1972 Stockholm UN Conference on the Human Environment, in which India took part.

q: The Government of India's policy on abatement of pollution adopted certain guiding principles in the year 1992. Which of the following is not covered under the said guiding principles?
o: Involvement of NGO's for all purposes
e: The 1992 Policy Statement for Abatement of Pollution covers source prevention, best available technology, polluter pays and public participation; it does not provide for NGO involvement 'for all purposes'.

q: Which one of the following is not the functions of Human Rights Council?
o: To promote Human Rights education and learning as well as advisory services
To decide issues without making any recommendations to the General Assembly
To work in close cooperation with the Government regional organisation, National Human rights institutions and civil society
To serve as forum for dialogue on thematic issues on all Human rights
e: The Human Rights Council makes recommendations to the General Assembly (e.g. on developing international human rights law); it does not decide issues without making recommendations.

q: 'Digital signature' is defined under which section of information technology Act, 2000?
e: Sec. 2(1)(p) of the IT Act, 2000 defines 'digital signature' as authentication of an electronic record by the means given in Sec. 3.

q: 'Cyber security' is defined under which section of information technology Act, 2000?
e: 'Cyber security' is defined in Sec. 2(1)(nb), inserted by the 2008 amendment.

q: The term private key refers to:
o: Authentication of any electronic record by a subscriber
Electronic signature certificate issued under section 35
Key pair in an asymmetric crypto system
Key of key pair used to create a digital signature
e: Sec. 2(1)(zc) IT Act defines 'private key' as the key of a key pair used to create a digital signature.

q: The validity of contracts formed through electronic means is contained under which section of information technology Act, 2000?
e: Sec. 10A (inserted in 2008) says a contract is not unenforceable merely because electronic means were used to form it.

q: The right to information Act, 2005 explains the meaning of information under:
e: Sec. 2(f) of the RTI Act defines 'information'. Sec. 2(h) is 'public authority' and 2(j) is 'right to information'.

q: The Lokpal and Lokayukta Act 2013 came in to force in:
e: The Act was passed in December 2013, received assent on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January 2014. Among the options, January is the nearest.
n: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act commenced on 16 January 2014 (assent 1 January 2014), but the paper says 2013. 'January' is kept as the closest option.

q: Which one of the following is related to Amendment of the U.S. constitution?
e: Article V of the U.S. Constitution lays down the amendment procedure. Article III is judiciary, IV is relations between States, VI is supremacy.

q: Section 8(1) of the RTI Act provides how many exemptions from the disclosure of information?
e: Sec. 8(1) lists ten exemptions, clauses (a) to (j).

q:
According to prof. Lon L Fuller:
(A) Law is the enterprise of subjecting human conduct to the governance of rules
(B) The morality of law has two aspects, external and internal
(C) External morality is the morality of aspiration, ideas from which it is possible to derive a procedural version of natural law
(D) Internal morality of law is a 'substantive version of natural law'
e: Fuller defined law as the enterprise of subjecting human conduct to rules and spoke of external and internal morality of law. His internal morality is a procedural version of natural law, so statements (C) and (D) are wrong.

q:
In which of the following cases the duties are not specifically enforced in respect of the act done?
(A) The liability of a borrower to repay a debt barred by statute of limitation
(B) The liability of a borrower to repay the money borrowed by him
(C) To refrain the wrong doer from publication when a libel has already been published
(D) To refrain the wrong doer to continue the commission of a nuisance
e: Duties of imperfect obligation such as a time-barred debt cannot be enforced, and an injunction cannot undo a libel already published. Repaying a loan and stopping a continuing nuisance are enforceable.

q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) Global justice inquires about justice among human beings consists in.
(B) Global justice inquiries take individual human beings as of primary concern and seek to give an account of what fairness among such agents involves.
(C) In the domain of global justice, theorists seek primarily to define justice between states or nations.
(D) In international justice the nation or state is taken as the central entity of concern and justice among nations or states is the focus.
e: Global justice centres on individuals as the primary concern (A, B), while international justice centres on states and justice between them (D). Statement (C) wrongly attributes the state-focus to global justice.

q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) The Preamble contains in nutshell ideals and aspirations of the Constitution
(B) The Preamble is the key to open the minds of the Constitution makers
(C) The Preamble to the Constitution of India is solemnly resolved to secure to its citizens justice and equity
(D) The Preamble is not the part of the Constitution
e: The Preamble summarises the Constitution's ideals and is the key to the makers' minds (A, B). It secures justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, not 'equity' (C), and since Kesavananda Bharati it is part of the Constitution (D).
n: Options A and D are identical in the original paper (both read '(A) and (B) only'). Either is correct.

q:
Which of the following statements are true under the Constitution of India?
(A) Article 61 deals with procedure for impeachment of the President
(B) Art 142 provides that law declared by the supreme court shall be biding on all courts
(C) Article 122 provides that courts shall not inquire into proceedings of Parliament
(D) Art 163 deals with the extent of executive power of State
e: Art. 61 (impeachment of President) and Art. 122 (courts not to inquire into Parliament's proceedings) are correct. The binding effect of Supreme Court law is in Art. 141 (Art. 142 is complete justice), and the State's executive power extent is in Art. 162 (Art. 163 is Council of Ministers).

q:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct?
(A) When a State is defeated or conquered, all the citizens acquire the Nationality of the conquering State. This is called 'cession' mode of gain of nationality.
(B) When a person gets Nationality of a State in place of the Nationality of another State. This is called 'substitution' mode of loss of nationality.
(C) The Public Trustee case is related to statelessness.
(D) The General Assembly decided to convene a conference to conclude, a convention on reduction of statelessness in 1961.
e: Acquiring nationality of a conqueror on conquest is 'subjugation', not 'cession', so (A) is wrong and every option containing (A) is out. 'Substitution' is a mode of loss of nationality (B) and the Public Trustee case concerned statelessness (C).

q:
Which of the following statement/statements, is/are correct?
(A) De Jure Recognition is final whereas De-facto Recognition is provisional
(B) De-Facto Recognition can be withdrawn but De-Jure Recognition is irrevocable
(C) De-Facto Recognition has retrospective operation as exactly as, in the case of De-Jure recognition
(D) There is no distinction between De-Jure and de Facto recognition for the purpose of giving effects to the internal acts of the recognised authority
e: De jure recognition is final and irrevocable while de facto recognition is provisional and can be withdrawn (A, B). For giving effect to the internal acts of the recognised authority there is no distinction between the two (D). Statement (C) is treated as incorrect in the published key.

q:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct?
(A) On 16th June, 1987 the foreign secretaries of South Asian Regional Countries entered into agreement on Extradition
(B) Hongkong Pact on Extradition with India was entered in the middle of June 1980
(C) India and Germany signed an Extradition Treaty on 27 June, 2001
(D) India and France signed an Extradition Treaty on 24 June, 2002
e: The India-Germany extradition treaty was signed on 27 June 2001 (C). The Hong Kong agreement dates from 1997 and the India-France treaty from January 2003, so (B) and (D) fail.

q:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct?
(A) The offence of abetment is defined under section 107 of IPC
(B) The essential ingredient of 'the offence of conspiracy is the agreement to commit an offence
(C) The punishment of criminal conspiracy is given under section 120 of IPC
(D) State of Tamil Nadu through Superintendent of Police, CBI/SIT V. Nalini is a case related to offence of Abetment
(E) Abetment in India of offences committed outside of India is punishable under section 108A IPC
e: Abetment is defined in Sec. 107, conspiracy requires an agreement (Sec. 120A), and Sec. 108A covers abetment in India of offences outside India. Conspiracy is punished under Sec. 120B (not 120), and the Nalini (Rajiv Gandhi assassination) case was mainly about criminal conspiracy.

q:
Which of the following statement/statements are correct?
(A) 'Theft' is defined under section 378 IPC, as the dishonest removal of movable property out of the possession of any person without his consent
(B) In the offence of extortion punishment is upto 3 years under section 384 IPC
(C) The offence of 'Robbery' is defined under section 391 IPC
(D) Dacoity is Robbery committed by five or more persons
(E) The punishment for 'Dacoity' is prescribed under section 392 IPC
e: Theft (Sec. 378), extortion (Sec. 384, up to 3 years) and dacoity as robbery by five or more persons are correct. Robbery is defined in Sec. 390 (391 is dacoity), and dacoity is punished under Sec. 395 (392 is punishment for robbery).

q:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct?
(A) The offence of 'sedition' is defined under section 124A of IPC
(B) The supreme court in Kedar Nath Singh V State of Bihar held that section 124A IPC is not unconstitutional
(C) State (N.C.T. of Delhi) V. Navjot Sandhu Afsan Guru is a case related to sedition
(D) Mohd. Arif V State of NCT of Delhi is also known as Mumbai Terror Attack case
(E) Waging or attempt to wage war or abetting waging of war against the Government of India is an offence under section 121 IPC.
e: Sec. 124A defined sedition, Kedar Nath Singh (1962) upheld it, and Sec. 121 punishes waging war. Navjot Sandhu was the Parliament attack case (not sedition) and Mohd. Arif was the Red Fort attack case, not the Mumbai attack.

q:
In determining relevant geographic market, competition commission shall keep in mind which of the following factors?
(A) Regulatory trade barriers and natural procurement policies
(B) Language and local specification requirement
(C) Consumer preference and regular supply and after sale service
(D) Transport and distribution factors
e: Sec. 19(6) of the Competition Act lists all of these: trade barriers, procurement policies, local specification, language, consumer preferences, supply and after-sales needs, transport costs and distribution facilities.

q:
Consumer, Mediation Cell has to hold which of the following documents?
(A) List of empanelled mediators
(B) List of all cases handled by the cell
(C) Records of all proceedings
(D) Information specified by regulations
e: Under Sec. 74 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a Consumer Mediation Cell maintains the mediator panel, the list of cases handled, records of proceedings and other information specified by regulations.

q:
Removal of members of Company Law Appellate Tribunal can be carried out in consultation by:
(A) Central Government
(B) Chief Justice
(C) Chairperson of Appellate tribunal
(D) Auditor General
e: Removal of Tribunal members is by the Central Government, after an inquiry and in consultation with the Chief Justice (of India), so options (A) and (B) apply.

q:
Endorsement of Negotiable instrument followed by delivery:
(A) Transfers the property in instrument to endorsee
(B) Transfers the right of further negotiation to the endorsee
(C) May exclude or restrict the right of further negotiation by endorsee
(D) May merely constitute the endorsee as an agent
e: Sec. 50 of the Negotiable Instruments Act: endorsement plus delivery transfers the property and right of further negotiation, but express words may restrict or exclude that right or make the endorsee a mere agent.

q:
Under Muslim Law, divorce by common consent is known as:
(A) Talaq-e-Tafwid
(B) Khula
(C) Lian
(D) Mubarat
e: Khula (initiated by the wife with consideration) and Mubarat (mutual desire to separate) are divorces by agreement. Talaq-e-Tafwid is delegated divorce and Lian is divorce on false accusation of adultery.

q:
Which of the following are fault grounds of divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955?
(A) Desertion
(B) Cruelty
(C) Consent obtained by force or fraud
(D) Conversion to non Hindu religion
e: Desertion, cruelty and conversion are fault grounds under Sec. 13(1). Consent obtained by force or fraud is a ground for annulling a voidable marriage under Sec. 12, not for divorce.

q:
Under the provisions of the Hindu succession Act, 1956
(A) Son of a predeceased daughter is class I heir
(B) Widow of a predeceased son of a pre-deceased son is class II heir
(C) Mother's mother is class I heir
(D) Mother's father is class II heir
e: A predeceased daughter's son is a Class I heir and the mother's father is Class II. The widow of a predeceased son of a predeceased son is Class I, and the mother's mother is Class II.

q:
The National Commission for Women shall perform some of the following functions:
(A) Shall fund litigations involving issues affecting a large body of women
(B) Shall provide, financial assistance to all those who are self employed
(C) Shall call for specific studies or investigation in to specific problems
(D) Shall impose punishment to those found involved in discrimination of women
(E) Shall investigate and examine all matters relating to the safeguards provided for women under the Constitution and other laws
e: Under Sec. 10 of the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 the Commission funds litigation on issues affecting many women, calls for special studies and investigates safeguards for women. It has no power to give financial aid to the self-employed or to punish.

q:
Examine the relevancy of class action suit and choose the correct answer:
(A) A class action would measurably assist in securing redress in Environmental cases
(B) Monetary recoveries from the tort feasors in environmental cases can only be obtained through a suit
(C) The writ procedure appears more suited than the class action procedure
(D) The most obvious use of class action is in the mass disasters of the sort that occurred in Bhopal
e: Class actions help secure redress in environmental harm, damages from wrongdoers need a suit, and mass disasters like Bhopal are the obvious use. Statement (C) argues against the relevance of class action, so it is excluded.

q:
The geographical indications are distinctive signs or indications which identify any goods as:
(A) Act of unfair competition under Paris convention, 1967
(B) Originating in a specified territory
(C) Stipulate the misleading test guaranteeing a negative right
(D) Specific quality, reputation and characteristics
(E) Essentially attributable to origin
e: Art. 22(1) of TRIPS: goods originating in a territory, where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic is essentially attributable to that geographical origin.

q:
Nothing in TRIPS agreement, 1995 shall derogate from the existing obligations prescribed under:
(A) Paris Convention, 1967
(B) Rome Convention, 1961
(C) Berne Convention, 1971
(D) Biodiversity Convention, 1992
(E) Integrated Circuit Treaty, 1989
e: Art. 2(2) of TRIPS preserves obligations under the Paris Convention, Berne Convention, Rome Convention and the Treaty on Intellectual Property in Respect of Integrated Circuits. The Biodiversity Convention is not listed.

q:
'Computer network' means the inter connection of one or more computers of computer systems or communication devices through:-
(A) The use of satellite, microwave, terrestrial line, wire, wireless or other communication media
(B) A device or collection of devices including input and output support devices
(C) Any electronic, magnetic, optical and other high speed data processing device
(D) All input, out, processing, storage, computer software or communication facilities
(E) Terminal or a complex consisting of two or more interconnected computers or communication device
e: Sec. 2(1)(j) of the IT Act, 2000 defines 'computer network' as inter-connection through (i) satellite, microwave, terrestrial line, wire, wireless or other communication media and (ii) terminals or a complex of two or more interconnected computers or communication devices.

q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) In Canada, the federation was not a voluntary union but was imposed by an Act
(B) In India, the Act of 1935 created autonomous units and forged them into a federation
(C) The American Union was formed by voluntary agreement among a number of sovereign states
(D) Indian constitution has been framed by the States and not by the people of India
e: Canada's federation came through the British North America Act, India's through the Government of India Act, 1935, and the US Union by agreement of sovereign states. The Indian Constitution was framed by a Constituent Assembly representing the people, not by the States.

q:
Amendment in the American constitution may by proposed by:-
(A) Congress with a 2/3 majority in both the Houses of Representatives and the Senate
(B) Congress with a 3/4 majority in both the Houses of Representatives and the Senate
(C) Constitutional convention called by two third of State Legislatures
(D) Constitutional convention called by three fourth of State Legislatures
e: Under Article V, amendments are proposed either by two-thirds of both Houses of Congress or by a convention called on the application of two-thirds of State legislatures. Three-fourths is needed for ratification, not proposal.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Books): (A) The Growth of the Law; (B) The Theory of Legal Science; (C) An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation; (D) The Law of Peoples
List II (Jurists): (I) H. Cairns; (II) Cardozo; (III) John Rawls; (IV) Jeremy Bentham
e: The Growth of the Law is by Cardozo, The Theory of Legal Science by Huntington Cairns, Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation by Bentham and The Law of Peoples by John Rawls.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Art 326 of the Constitution; (B) Art 324(3) of the Constitution; (C) Art 328 of the Constitution; (D) Art 329 of the Constitution
List II: (I) Chief Election Commissioner shall act as the chairman of the Election Commission; (II) Ban to interference by courts in electoral matters; (III) Elections to be on the basis of adult suffrage; (IV) Power of Legislature of a State to make provisions with respect to elections to such Legislature
e: Art. 326 provides adult suffrage, Art. 324(3) makes the CEC chairman of the Election Commission, Art. 328 empowers State legislatures on their elections and Art. 329 bars court interference in electoral matters.

q:
Match List I with List II (Conferences of W.T.O.):
List I: (A) Third Ministerial Conference of WTO was held at; (B) Sixth Ministerial Conference of WTO was held at; (C) Fourth Ministerial Conference of WTO was held at; (D) Seventh Ministerial Conference of WTO was held at
List II (Places): (I) Hong Kong (China); (II) Seattle (US); (III) Geneva (Switzerland); (IV) Doha (Qatar)
e: Third Ministerial: Seattle (1999); Fourth: Doha (2001); Sixth: Hong Kong (2005); Seventh: Geneva (2009).

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Definitions of): (A) Solitary confinement; (B) Act of a child under seven years of age; (C) Communication made in good faith; (D) Act causing slight harm
List II (Provisions of Indian Penal Code): (I) Section 95 IPC; (II) Section 93; (III) Section 73 IPC; (IV) Section 82 IPC
e: Sec. 73 covers solitary confinement, Sec. 82 acts of a child under seven, Sec. 93 communication made in good faith and Sec. 95 acts causing slight harm.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Negligence; (B) Strict liability; (C) Absolute liability; (D) Nervous shock
List II: (I) Ryland V Fletcher; (II) M.C. Mehta V Union of India; (III) Glasgow corporation vs Muir; (IV) Bourhill V Young
e: Glasgow Corporation v. Muir is a negligence case, Rylands v. Fletcher gave strict liability, M.C. Mehta gave absolute liability, and Bourhill v. Young dealt with nervous shock.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Section 162 of the Indian contract Act, 1872; (B) Section 178 of the Indian contract Act 1872; (C) Section 214 of the India contract Act, 1872; (D) Section 150 of the Indian contract Act, 1872
List II: (I) Pledge by Mercantile Agent; (II) Bailor's duty to disclose faults in goods bailed; (III) Termination of gratuitous bailment by death; (IV) Agent's duty to communicate with principal
e: Sec. 162 ends a gratuitous bailment on death of bailor or bailee, Sec. 178 deals with pledge by a mercantile agent, Sec. 214 with an agent's duty to communicate with the principal, Sec. 150 with the bailor's duty to disclose faults.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Sec.13 of C.P.C.; (B) Sec.2(5) of C.P.C.; (C) Sec. 2(6) of C.P.C.; (D) Sec.14 of C.P.C.
List II: (I) Foreign court; (II) Presumption as to foreign judgements; (III) When foreign judgement not conclusive; (IV) Judgement of a foreign court
e: Sec. 13 CPC lists when a foreign judgment is not conclusive, Sec. 2(5) defines 'foreign court', Sec. 2(6) defines 'foreign judgment' and Sec. 14 raises a presumption as to foreign judgments.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) National Human Rights Commission; (B) National Commission for Backward Class; (C) National Commission for Minorities; (D) National Commission for Scheduled Caste
List II: (I) Article 338; (II) State to introduce regulatory regime in the National Interest; (III) Power to recommend payment of compensation; (IV) Article 338-B

q:
Match List I with List II (Definitions under the Information Technology Act, 2000):

List II: (I) Section 2(g); (II) Section 2(k); (III) Section 2(j); (IV) Section 2(i)
e: Under Sec. 2(1) of the IT Act: computer is (i), computer network (j), computer resource (k) and Certifying Authority (g).

q:

List II: (I) Presidential Election Nov.7, 2012; (II) Congress on the eve of Presidential Election; (III) The Judicial power in American Supreme Court; (IV) Amendment of the Constitutions
e: Article V of the U.S. Constitution deals with the amendment of the Constitution and Article III with the judicial power of the Supreme Court. The chapter items complete the match as in option 3.

q:
Arrange in chronological order the publication of the books on Jurisprudence:
(A) A Practical Treatise of Architectural Jurisprudence by James Elmes
(B) The Spirit of Common Law by Roscoe Pound
(C) World Poverty and Human Rights by Thomas Pogge
(D) Taking Rights Seriously by Ronald Dworkin
(E) The Growth of the Law by Benjamin N. Cardozo
e: Elmes (1827), Pound's Spirit of the Common Law (1921), Cardozo's Growth of the Law (1924), Dworkin's Taking Rights Seriously (1977), Pogge's World Poverty and Human Rights (2002).

q:
Chronologically arrange (Article wise) the following provisions of the Constitution of India:
(A) Special Provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim
(B) Special Provisions with respect to the State of Karnataka
(C) Special Provisions with respect to the State of Manipur
(D) Special Provisions with respect to the State of Nagaland
e: Article order: Nagaland 371A, Manipur 371C, Sikkim 371F, Karnataka 371J (added by the 98th Amendment, 2012).

q:
Indicate the correct chronological order of years the following cases they were decided:
(A) Case concerning the Temple of Preah Vihear
(B) Frontier Dispute (Burkina Faso V. Mali)
(C) The Caroline case
(D) R.V. Keyn
(E) Chorzow factory (Indemnity) case
e: The Caroline case (1837), R v. Keyn (1876), Chorzow Factory (1928), Temple of Preah Vihear (1962), Frontier Dispute Burkina Faso v. Mali (1986).

q:
Indicate the chronological order of the years of the following cases as decided by the Supreme Court:
(A) State of T.N. V. Balkrishna
(B) Mangesh V. State of Maharashtra
(C) Ram Kumar V. State of M.P.
(D) K.M. Nanavati V State of Maharashtra
(E) Mahesh chander V. State of Delhi
e: Chronological order of decision as per the published answer key: K.M. Nanavati (1961) comes first, followed by State of T.N. v. Balakrishna, Mangesh, Ram Kumar and Mahesh Chander in that order.

q:
Arrange the correct sequence in which the liability for tort will arise for the following:
(A) Damages
(B) Breach of duty
(C) Duty to take care
(D) Causation
e: Negligence is established in sequence: a duty of care, breach of that duty, causation (the breach caused the harm), and resulting damage.

q:
Arrange the provisions of the Indian contract Act 1872 in chronological order (Section wise):
(A) Who are competent to contract
(B) Effect of mistakes as to law
(C) What agreements are contracts
(D) Agreement in restraint of marriage is void
e: Section order: Sec. 10 (what agreements are contracts), Sec. 11 (who are competent), Sec. 21 (mistake of law), Sec. 26 (agreement in restraint of marriage void).

q:
Arrange in chronological order the following judgments on cruelty as a ground of divorce:
(A) A. Jaya Chandra V. Aneel Kaur
(B) Naveen Kohli V. Neelu Kohli
(C) Dastane V. Dastane
(D) Bhagat V. Bhagat
e: Dastane v. Dastane (1975), Bhagat v. Bhagat (1994), A. Jayachandra v. Aneel Kaur (2005), Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli (2006).

q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) United Nation Conference on the Human Environment
(B) United Nation Conference on Sustainable Development
(C) United Nations Conference on Environment and Development
(D) World Commission on Environment and Development
(E) United Nations Sustainable Development
e: Stockholm Conference (1972), World Commission on Environment and Development (Brundtland, 1983-87), Earth Summit (1992), Rio+20 Conference on Sustainable Development (2012), UN Sustainable Development Summit and Goals (2015).

q:
Prof. William Fisher identified four analytical constructs of theories of intellectual property under which of the following sequence?
(A) Personality Theory
(B) Labour Theory
(C) Social Planning Theory
(D) Utilitarian Theory
e: Fisher's four theories, in his usual order: utilitarian, labour (Lockean), personality (Hegelian) and social planning.

q:
The trend towards codification of the British constitution in whole or in part is a movement during the past decade from eminent quarters. Arrange them in chronological order:
(A) Northern Ireland Act
(B) Referendum Act
(C) Scotland Act
(D) European Communities Act
e: European Communities Act (1972), Northern Ireland constitutional legislation (1973-74), Referendum Act (1975), Scotland Act (1978).

q:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion A: The rule making power of the Supreme Court for regulating the practice and procedure of the court is not subject to any law made by the Parliament of India
Reason R: Only an impartial and independent judiciary can protect the right of individual without fear or favor
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
e: Art. 145 makes the Supreme Court's rule-making power 'subject to any law made by Parliament', so A is false. R is a true statement about judicial independence.

q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reasons R.
Assertion A: The right of private defence of body extends to causing of death to the Assailant in case of assault of throwing or administering acid or an attempt to throw or administer acid which may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequences of such Act.
Reason R: This provision was inserted under clause (7) of section 100 IPC by Act 13 of 2013 in view of increasing cases of acid throwing on the girls and women in India
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
e: The seventh clause of Sec. 100 IPC, inserted by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 (Act 13 of 2013), allows causing death in defence against acid attack. It was added because of rising acid attacks, so R explains A.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Dominant position means position of strength enjoyed by an enterprise in relevant market in India which enables it to operate independently of operative forces and affects competitors and consumers in its favour.
Statement II: No enterprise shall abuse its dominant position.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
e: Sec. 4 of the Competition Act, 2002 (with its Explanation) defines dominant position as such strength in the relevant market, and Sec. 4(1) prohibits abuse of it.

q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reasons R.
Assertion A: Under the companies Act of 2013 Central Government is authorised to implement a facility to file documents in electronic form.
Reason R: Central Government is authorised to make rules to implement this facility and section 398, 401 and 402 have been incorporated in the Act of 2013.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
e: The Companies Act, 2013 provides for electronic filing of documents (Chapter XXIX, including Secs. 398 and 402), and the Central Government makes rules to put this facility in place, which explains the assertion.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: No person except the father or mother of a child shall have the capacity to give the child in adoption under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956.
Statement II: Under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956, the same child may not be adopted simultaneously by two or more persons
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
e: Under Sec. 9, a guardian (with court permission) can also give a child in adoption, so Statement I is wrong. Sec. 11 bars adoption of the same child simultaneously by two or more persons, so Statement II is correct.

q:
Read the given passage and answer the question that follows. (Passage on the right to privacy: privacy is an essential aspect of dignity; it has not been expressed as an independent fundamental right but lies across the spectrum of protected freedoms.)
The referred paragraph is taken from the judgement of the Supreme Court in

Maneka Gandhi V. Union of India
Justice K.S. Puttaswami (Retd.) and another V. Union of India and others

The referred paragraph is a part of the judgement delivered by:
e: This passage appears in the plurality opinion of Justice D.Y. Chandrachud in Puttaswamy (2017).

q:

In which of the following case it was held that right to privacy is not protected as a fundamental right under the Constitution?
o: M.P, Sharma V. Satish Chandra, District Magistrate, Delhi
R. Rajagopal V. State of Tamil Nadu
K.S. Puttaswami V. Union of India
e: M.P. Sharma v. Satish Chandra (1954, eight judges) held there is no fundamental right to privacy against search and seizure. It was overruled by Puttaswamy.

q:
Read the given passage and answer the question that follows. (Passage on the right to privacy as an essential aspect of dignity.)
In which of the following case it was held that the procedure established by law means the procedure must be just, fair and reasonable?
o: Kharak Singh V. State of U.P
A.K. Gopalan V. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi V. Union of India
e: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) held that 'procedure established by law' in Art. 21 must be just, fair and reasonable, not arbitrary.

q:
Read the given passage and answer the question that follows. (Passage on the right to privacy as an essential aspect of dignity.)
Which one of the following statement is correct?
o: Right to privacy is expressly provided as a fundamental right under the Constitution
Right to privacy is protected as a fundamental right under Article 21 of the constitution
Right to privacy is not protected as a fundamental right under Article 21of the constitution
Article 21 of the constitution protects the life and personal liberty only from executive action
e: Puttaswamy (2017) held that privacy is a constitutionally protected right, intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Art. 21 and to Part III freedoms, though not expressly mentioned.

According to Austin, the positive law has following three attributes:

q:
Read the passage carefully (passage on the binding force of international law and its relation to natural law and morality) and answer the question that follows.
Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: Starke and Kelsen contend that there is both legislation and law enforcement in international law
According to Starke, legislation being provided by multilateral treaties in international law
According to Kelsen, sanctions are provided by the right of self-help and war in international law
Treaties and self-help can qualify as legislation and law-enforcement in a positivist sense
e: Starke and Kelsen see treaties as a form of legislation and self-help and war as sanction (A to C). The claim that they qualify in a strict positivist sense is the incorrect one, since international law has no central legislature or enforcer.

q:
Read the passage carefully (passage on the binding force of international law and its relation to natural law and morality) and answer the question that follows.
Who defines law 'as a body of rules for human conduct within a community, which by common consent of this community shall be enforced by external power?
e: This is Oppenheim's definition of law, which is why he regarded international law as true law.

q:
Read the passage carefully (passage on the binding force of international law and its relation to natural law and morality) and answer the question that follows.
Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: Hart's analysis of law suggests that international law consists of legal rules forming not a system but a set of rules.
The absence in international law of any basic rules of recognition prevents its being unified into a system
International law remains a mere set of separate rules
Many of the rules of international law rest on treaty, not on custom
e: Hart observed that many rules of international law rest on custom, not treaty. The other statements correctly reflect his view that it is a set of rules without a rule of recognition.

q:
Read the passage carefully (passage on the binding force of international law and its relation to natural law and morality) and answer the question that follows.
The view that international law consisted of the precepts dictated to States by natural law was advanced by:
e: Emmerich de Vattel's 'necessary law of nations' treated international law as precepts of natural law dictated to States.

Which theory of learning supports reflective level of teaching?
e: The reflective level of teaching is problem-centred and promotes insight and thinking, which fits cognitive (field) theories rather than the behaviourist conditioning and reinforcement theories.

q:
Identify the characteristics of field-dependent learners from the following:
(A) Perceives global aspects of concepts and materials
(B) Focuses on facts and principles
(C) Prefers to work alone
(D) Seeks guidance and demonstration from teacher
(E) Likes to cooperate
e: Field-dependent learners see the whole picture globally, need guidance and external structure from the teacher, and prefer cooperative, social learning. Focus on facts and working alone suit field-independent learners.

q:
Match List I (Levels of teaching and learning) with List II (Main feature):
(A) Autonomous development level; (B) Memory level; (C) Understanding level; (D) Reflective level
(I) It is problem-centred and requires on the part of learners more active participation, more imagination and creativeness; (II) Lays stress on the importance of students' feelings and minimizes the value of hard thinking; (III) It is comparatively thoughtless; (IV) It emphasizes on seeing of relationships between principles and solitary facts.
e: Autonomous development stresses feelings, the memory level is thoughtless, the understanding level sees relationships between principles and facts, and the reflective level is problem-centred and creative.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Knowledge, comprehension and application levels in Bloom's taxonomy belong to the higher level of cognitive learning.
Statement II: Organization and characterization belong to higher level of affective outcomes.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
e: Knowledge, comprehension and application are lower-order cognitive levels, so Statement I is wrong. Organization and characterization are the highest levels of the affective domain, so Statement II is right.

q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Formative assessment is process linked and directed at raising motivation and engagement levels in learning.
Reason (R): The purpose of formative assessment is to improve quality of learning outcomes.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
e: Formative assessment is ongoing and aims to improve learning quality, and it does so by raising motivation and engagement, so R explains A.

q: Creating purpose statements, research questions and hypotheses that are narrow and measurable would mark the characteristic features of which research type?
e: Narrow, measurable hypotheses are typical of quantitative, experimental research. Narrative, ethnographic and grounded theory studies are qualitative and open-ended.

q:
In 'two groups, randomized subjects post test only' research design which of the following may be the source for jeopardizing validity?
(A) Pretesting procedures
(B) Measuring instruments
(C) Interaction of selection and the independent variable
(D) Reactive experimental procedures
(E) Statistical regression
e: With randomisation and no pretest, pretesting effects and regression are controlled. External validity can still be threatened by selection-treatment interaction and reactive experimental procedures.

q:
Match List I (Research Steps) with List II (Main features):
(A) Defining a research problem; (B) Hypothesis making; (C) Drawing a research sample; (D) Hypothesis testing
(I) Appropriate statistical techniques for data analysis; (II) Representativeness of the units chosen; (III) Identifying the variables for setting up a plausible relationship; (IV) Carefully chosen terms and concepts with operational descriptions, if need be.
e: A problem needs clearly defined terms; a hypothesis identifies variables and their relationship; a sample must be representative; testing a hypothesis needs suitable statistical techniques.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Research ethics forms a genuine concern for research to lend credibility in findings.
Statement II: Use of ICT in research is mandatory as it is economical in terms of time and use of resources.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
e: Ethics lends credibility to research findings. ICT is helpful and efficient but not mandatory.

q:
Given below are two statements: One is labeled as Assertion A and the other is labeled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Format and styles of referencing in thesis writing are enforced with a view to effect observance of formal protocols.
Reason (R): Formal protocols ensure avoidance of deviations from norms and procedures of reporting research.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
e: Referencing formats are enforced to keep to formal protocols, and those protocols exist to prevent deviation from reporting norms, so R explains A.

q: The least contributor to noise in communication system by the audience is
e: Audience noise comes from selective exposure/attention, perception and retention. 'Selective intention' is not a recognised audience filter, so it contributes least.

q:
Which of the following are parameters of an effective communication?
(A) Freedom to see and hear. What is here?
(B) Freedom to say. What one thinks and feels?
(C) Freedom to decide. What should be, was, are, will be?
(D) Freedom to feel. What one feels?
(E) Freedom of always waiting for permission.
e: Virginia Satir's freedoms for open communication include seeing and hearing what is here, saying what one thinks and feels, and feeling what one feels. Deciding what 'should be' and always waiting for permission are not among them.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Communication is the process of transmitting a message from a source to an audience via a channel.
Statement II: To establish 'Commonness' between the source and the audience is effective for success of communication.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
e: Communication is the transmission of a message from source to receiver through a channel, and shared meaning ('commonness') is essential for it to succeed.

q:
Match List I (Styles that impede communications) with List II (Characteristic feature):
(A) Placating; (B) Blaming; (C) Computing; (D) Distracting
(I) Doing or saying what is irrelevant; (II) Being overcorrect; (III) Fault finding and acting as superior; (IV) Talking in an ingratiating way
e: In Satir's communication stances: placating is ingratiating, blaming is fault-finding from a superior position, computing is overcorrect and intellectual, distracting is irrelevant.

q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): More effective communication occurs when source and receiver are homophilous.
Reason (R): Source and receiver use same language and words to stimulate similar meaning.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
e: Homophily means similarity between source and receiver; sharing language and words produces similar meaning, which is why it improves communication.

q: A milkman has been mixing water with milk to earn 25 per cent profit by selling the mixture at the cost price. The ratio of water and milk, respectively, is?
e: Selling the mixture at the cost price of pure milk means the profit comes from the water. If 100 parts milk give 125 parts mixture, then 25 parts of water are added, a ratio of 25:100 = 1:4.

q: A 12 percent debt instrument yields 20 percent return. The market price of the underlying debt instrument is
e: Yield = coupon / market price. Taking face value Rs. 100, coupon = Rs. 12, so market price = 12/0.20 = Rs. 60.

q: The difference between the simple interest received from two different sources on Rs. 1,500 for three years is Rs. 13.50. The difference between their rates of interest is
e: Difference in interest = 1500 x 3 x d / 100 = 13.50, so 45d = 13.50 and d = 0.3%.

q: A watch reads 4.30. If the minute hand points East, in which direction will the hour hand point?
e: At 4:30 the minute hand is at 6, and the hour hand is midway between 4 and 5, which is 135 degrees clockwise from 12. If 6 points East then 12 points West, and 135 degrees clockwise from West is North-East.

q: In a certain code language, 24685 is written as 33776. How is 35791 written in that code?
e: The code adds 1, subtracts 1, adds 1, subtracts 1, adds 1 to the digits in turn (2,4,6,8,5 gives 3,3,7,7,6). So 3,5,7,9,1 gives 4,4,8,8,2.

q: According to Nyaya the argument - 'Sound is eternal because it is produced' commits which of the following fallacy?
e: Being produced implies non-eternity, so the reason proves the opposite of the thesis. This is the fallacy of viruddha (contradictory reason).

q:
With reference to pramana theory both on dialogical and philosophical discourse, which of the following options are correct?
(A) It furnishes the required grounding for the thesis to be backed up by a certain means of knowledge.
(B) It provides the necessary platform to incisely analyse the proposed thesis.
(C) It enables us to succinctly summarise the observations, that stem out of analysis, in the form of anumana or nyaya prayoga.
(D) It enables the debater to elicit acceptance of his/her own belief system on the basis of formal validity alone.
e: Pramana theory grounds a thesis in a means of knowledge, gives a platform for analysing it and lets the findings be summarised as inference. It is not meant to win acceptance of one's own beliefs by formal validity alone.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The works in Nyaya-Sastra discuss the aggregate causal conditions and the process involved in inferential cognition.
Statement II: The works in Nyaya-Sastra do not however dwell upon analysis of the factors that help to assess and decide the formal validity of a judgement.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
e: Nyaya works do treat the causal conditions and process of inference, and they also analyse the factors that decide the validity of a judgement (for example hetvabhasa, the fallacies of reasoning), so Statement II is incorrect.

q: "Famous Singer Himanshu says that Coffeehill chocolates are groovy. We can only conclude that Coffeehill chocolates are groovy indeed". Which of the fallacy is committed in the above statement?
e: A singer is not an authority on chocolates; relying on his opinion as proof is an appeal to unqualified authority.

q:
The set of attributes shared by all and only those objects to which a general term refers, is called:
(A) The intension of that term
(B) Connotation of that term
(C) The extension of that term
(D) Denotation of that term
e: The attributes that define a term are its intension, also called connotation. Extension (denotation) is the set of objects to which the term applies.

q:
With regard to computer memory, which of the following statements are TRUE?
(A) Secondary storage is slower, cheaper, and less volatile than primary storage.
(B) Tape drives are direct access devices.
(C) The contents of most forms of RAM are volatile, thus making them unsuitable for long term data storage.
e: Secondary storage is slower, cheaper and non-volatile compared with primary memory, and RAM loses its contents without power. Tape drives are sequential access, not direct access.

q: With respect to computers, what is the main advantage of a Graphical User Interface (GUI) compared with a Command Line Interface (CLI)?
o: Provides higher level of security and requires less memory
Performs complex tasks faster and requires less memory
e: A GUI uses icons, windows and menus, so non-experts can use it without learning commands. It generally needs more memory and processing power than a CLI.

q:
Identify the correct order of the following computer storage capacities ranked from smallest to largest capacity.
(A) 100 GBytes
(B) 10 000 000 000 Bytes
(C) 1 TBytes
(D) 100 000 MBytes
(E) 1 000 000 KBytes
e: Converted: (E) 1 GB, (B) 10 GB, (D) 100 GB, (A) 100 GB and (C) 1000 GB (1 TB). So the order is E, B, D, A, C (D and A are equal in size).

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: A web browser is a piece of software that retrieves and displays web pages.
Statement II: A search engine is a special kind of website that helps people in finding web pages from other web-sites.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
e: A browser fetches and renders web pages, and a search engine is a website that indexes other sites and helps users find pages.

q:
Match List I (Computer Components) with List II (Description):
(A) HDD; (B) RAM; (C) ROM; (D) CRT
(I) Visual Display Unit; (II) Volatile Memory; (III) External Memory; (IV) Non-Writable Memory
