(C) T. N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India
(D) Tarun Bharat Sangh v. Union of India
e: The Doon Valley limestone quarrying case (R.L.E.K., Dehradun) was the first major Indian case on development versus ecological balance.

q:
Which of the following statement is not correct as per Austin on Law and Morality?
(A) Positive Laws are set by political superiors and are proper subject matter of jurisprudence
(B) Laws by analogy are laws improperly so called
(C) Command, Duty, Sanction and Morality are inseparable
(D) Laws are of two types: laws properly so called and laws improperly so called
(E) Austin's conception of law takes into account positive law and positive morality
e: Austin separated law from morality, so saying that command, duty, sanction and morality are inseparable is wrong; the other statements reflect his view.

q: Under Public International Law, the Nottebohm case is of great relevance in relation to which of the given options?
e: Nottebohm (Liechtenstein v. Guatemala, 1955) set the 'genuine link' test for diplomatic protection based on nationality.

q: Which of the following are the dates in which India signed and ratified the 1949 Geneva Conventions?
o: Signed on 10th December 1949 and ratified on 13th November, 1950
Signed on 15th August 1949 and ratified on 26th January, 1950
Signed on 16th December 1949 and ratified on 9th November, 1950
Signed on 1st January 1949 and ratified on 10th December, 1950
e: India signed the 1949 Geneva Conventions on 16 December 1949 and ratified them on 9 November 1950.

q:
Which of the following analysis is NOT true for 5th Cent. BC Greek play of Antigone by Sophocles?
(A) Antigone followed and supported natural law over legal positivism, that is, right to bury
(B) Duties towards family v. State
(C) An early and undeveloped site of civil disobedience
(D) Irrationality of women's arbitrary subjectivity v. male state expressed through the duty to formal law
(E) Antigone was excused by State on humanitarian basis
e: In the play Antigone is condemned by Creon and entombed, not excused on humanitarian grounds, so (E) is untrue.

q:
Which statements are true about theories of corporate personality?
(A) Fiction theory says only human beings can be properly called persons
(B) Concession theory states that corporate bodies have legal personality only if granted by Law
(C) Fiction theory is also called 'Organic Theory'
(D) Symbolist or Brackets Theory says members of the corporations are only persons who have rights and duties
(E) Savigny, Salmond and Dicey support Fiction Theory
e: Fiction, concession, bracket (symbolist) theories and the Savigny/Salmond/Dicey support are correctly stated; 'organic theory' is the realist (Gierke) view, not fiction theory.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Concepts/Doctrines): (A) Lifting the corporate veil; (B) Invitation to public in the context of prospectus; (C) Doctrine of ultra vires; (D) Doctrine of indoor management
List II (Cases): (I) Nash v. Lynde; (II) Ashbury Rly Carriage and Iron Co. Ltd. v. Riche; (III) Royal British Bank v. Turquand; (IV) Salomon v. Salomon
e: Salomon is the corporate veil case, Nash v. Lynde the prospectus 'invitation to the public' case, Ashbury the ultra vires case and Turquand the indoor management case.

q:
Arrange the following grounds for dissolution of marriage in chronological order as stated in Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939?
(A) Husband has failed to provide for her maintenance for 2 years
(B) Husband has been insane for a period of two years
(C) Husband was impotent at the time of marriage and continues to be so
(D) Husband attempts to force her to lead immoral life
(E) Husband associates with women of evil repute
e: Sec. 2 of the 1939 Act lists failure to maintain (ii), impotence (v), insanity (vi), then cruelty heads including associating with women of evil repute and forcing an immoral life.

q:
Which of the following is true with WTO?
(A) WTO is headquartered in Hague
(B) There has been 9 rounds of trade negotiation since the second world war
(C) Doha round is the latest round of negotiation for trade for WTO members
(D) WTO has 154 members
e: Eight GATT rounds plus the Doha Round make nine, and Doha is the latest; the WTO sits in Geneva and has more than 154 members.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (IPR Theory): (A) Personhood Theory; (B) Natural Right Theory; (C) Incentive Theory; (D) Creative Destruction Theory
List II (Proponents/Jurists/Writers): (I) John Locke; (II) Joseph Schumpeter; (III) Immanuel Kant; (IV) William Nordhaus
e: Personhood theory draws on Kant/Hegel, natural rights on Locke, the incentive theory on Nordhaus and creative destruction on Schumpeter.

q: Which of the following is the Schedule II of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010?
o: Heads under which compensation or relief for damage may be claimed
Rules to be followed by NGT
e: The Second Schedule of the NGT Act lists the heads under which compensation or relief for damage may be claimed.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Conference/Treaty/Convention/Protocol): (A) UN Conference on Environment and Development; (B) Kyoto Conference on Global Warming; (C) Paris Agreement; (D) Montreal Protocol
List II (Year): (I) 1987; (II) 1992; (III) 1997; (IV) 2015
e: UNCED (Rio) 1992, Kyoto Protocol 1997, Paris Agreement 2015, Montreal Protocol 1987.

q:
Arrange the following provisions of the Hague Convention, 1907 in the numerical order in which they appear:
(A) The Pacific Settlement of International Disputes
(B) The Limitation of Employment of Force for Recovery of Contract Debts
(C) The Opening of Hostilities
(D) The Laws and Customs of War on land
(E) The Rights and Duties of Neutral Power and Persons in case of War on Land
e: The 1907 Hague Conventions are numbered I (Pacific Settlement), II (Contract Debts), III (Opening of Hostilities), IV (Land War) and V (Neutral Powers on Land).

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Offence): (A) Gang rape; (B) Dacoity; (C) Kidnapping for Ransom; (D) Dowry death
List II (Punishment): (I) Any fine imposed shall be paid to the victim; (II) Punishable with death or imprisonment for life; (III) Not less than 7 years but may extend to imprisonment for life; (IV) Imprisonment for life
e: Gang rape: fine paid to the victim; dacoity: imprisonment for life; kidnapping for ransom: death or life imprisonment; dowry death: 7 years to life.

q: Which kind of encumbrance on property gives a right for the limited use of a piece of land to a person/persons without giving them possession of the land?
e: A servitude (easement) gives a limited right to use another's land without possession; a lease transfers possession.

q: Which one of the following is not part of Specified Dower in Muslim Law?
e: Specified dower is fixed in the contract (prompt or deferred); proper dower is payable when no amount was specified.

q:
The case of Vardhaman Kaushik v. Union of India decided in 2014-15 is considered unique in the context of resolving the menace of air pollution in Delhi because:
(A) The National Green Tribunal rejected the petition for want of locus standi for the petitioner
(B) The National Green Tribunal adopted the pragmatic "consultative and deliberated" approach in this case
(C) The National Green Tribunal rejected the petition for want of jurisdiction in the matter
(D) The National Green Tribunal permitted the burning of crop remnant in agricultural fields falling in NCR Delhi
e: In Vardhaman Kaushik the NGT adopted a consultative, pragmatic approach to Delhi's air pollution rather than dismissing the petition or permitting crop burning.

q:
Arrange the following Conventions/treaties in their chronological order.
(A) Hague Conventions (on humanitarian law)
(B) European Convention of Human Rights
(C) Geneva Convention
(D) Tokyo Convention (on hijacking)
(E) Universal Declaration of Human Rights
e: Hague Conventions (1899/1907), UDHR (1948), Geneva Conventions (1949), ECHR (1950), Tokyo Convention (1963).

q:
Which of the following statements are true in the context of form of government in USA and India?
(A) USA Constitution Sec. 7 gives President veto power over the bills passed by the Congress which can be further countered by 2/3 majority in both Houses
(B) U.S. and India strictly follow the doctrine of separation of powers
(C) The U.S. President is more powerful as compared to the Indian Prime Minister
(D) Removal method of USA President and Indian Prime Minister is technical and difficult
(E) U.S. President is not the member of legislature.
e: The presidential veto is overridable by two-thirds of both Houses, the US President is more powerful and is not a legislator; India does not follow strict separation of powers.

q:
Arrange the following International Conventions/Agreements in the chronological order of their adoption.
(A) Additional Protocols to the Geneva Conventions
(B) International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of all Migrant Workers and Members of their Families
(C) Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees
(D) Agreement establishing World Trade Organisation
e: Refugee Convention (1951), Additional Protocols (1977), Migrant Workers Convention (1990), WTO Agreement (1994).

q:
Arrange the following in order (section wise) as stated in chapter XVII of Indian Penal Code, 1860?
(A) Mischief
(B) Stolen property
(C) Making preparation to commit dacoity
(D) Dacoity with Murder
(E) Assembling for purpose of committing dacoity
e: By section: dacoity with murder (396), making preparation (399), assembling for dacoity (402), stolen property (410) and mischief (425).

q: Which of the following is not a 'fair dealing' under the Copyright Act?
e: Sec. 52 protects private use, research, criticism and reporting current events; commercial use is not a fair dealing purpose.

q: Which of the following statutes define 'person interested'?
e: Sec. 2(1)(t) of the Patents Act, 1970 defines 'person interested'.

q: In the context of refugees, which of the following options provide the analogous Article of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights corresponding to Article 3 of the ECHR?
e: Article 3 ECHR (prohibition of torture and inhuman treatment) corresponds to Article 4 of the EU Charter.

q:
Arrange the following provisions as per the correct order in the Indian Constitution.
(A) Executive Power of State
(B) Term of office of Governor
(C) Appointment of Governor
(D) Qualifications for Appointment as Governor
(E) Governor of State
e: Art. 153 (Governor), 154 (executive power), 155 (appointment), 156 (term of office), 157 (qualifications).

q: "Implied conditions as to quality or fitness of goods" is given under which section of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930?
e: Sec. 16 deals with implied conditions as to quality or fitness; Sec. 14 deals with title and Sec. 15 with sale by description or sample.

q:
In order to constitute a 'marz-ul-maut', which of the following conditions must be satisfied?
(A) The malady or illness must result in the death
(B) The illness must cause reasonable apprehension of death in the mind of donor
(C) There should be some external indicia of a serious illness
(D) There must be an apprehension of death in the mind of physician
(E) Delivery of possession must be given to the donee
e: Marz-ul-maut requires an illness ending in death, the donor's apprehension of death and external indicia of serious illness; delivery of possession is needed for the gift made in it.

q: What is the meaning of the following maxim? "Ex turpi causa non oritur actio"
o: From an immoral cause no action arises
From an immoral cause an action arises
From a moral cause an action arises
From a moral cause no action arises
e: The maxim means no action arises from an immoral (illegal) cause.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Relief under IPR suits): (A) Anton Piller Order; (B) Mareva Injunction; (C) John Doe Order; (D) Dynamic Injunction
List II (Concept): (I) Legal action against unknown parties; (II) Right to search premises and seize evidence without prior warning; (III) Injunction order against all mirror websites; (IV) Freezing of defendant's assets
e: Anton Piller allows search and seizure, Mareva freezes assets, John Doe targets unknown defendants and a dynamic injunction covers mirror websites.

q: Who among the following is currently (January, 2025) serving as Judge of International Court of Justice?
e: Dalveer Bhandari has served on the ICJ since 2012 and was re-elected for a further term.

q: What is the official language of International Court of Justice (ICJ)?
e: Under Art. 39 of the ICJ Statute the official languages are French and English.

q:
Arrange the following grounds in chronological order where Hindu wife is entitled to claim maintenance while living separately from her husband as stated in Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956.
(A) If he is guilty of Desertion
(B) If he has any other wife living
(C) If he has ceased to be a Hindu
(D) If he keeps a concubine in the same house
(E) If any other cause justifying her living separately
e: Sec. 18(2) lists desertion, cruelty, leprosy, another wife living, a concubine in the same house, conversion, then any other justifying cause.

q:
Which of the following cases are related to Restitution of Conjugal Rights according to Hindu Marriage Act, 1955?
(A) T. Sareetha v. Venkatasubbaiah
(B) Parkash v. Parmeshwari
(C) Tirath v. Kripal Singh
(D) Harvinder Kaur v. Harmander Singh
(E) Sureshtha Devi v. Om Prakash
e: Sareetha, Parkash, Tirath Kaur and Harvinder Kaur are restitution of conjugal rights cases; Sureshtha Devi concerns mutual-consent divorce.

q: The limitation of the doctrine of constructive notice is known as which of the following?
e: The doctrine of indoor management (Turquand's rule) limits constructive notice: outsiders may assume internal formalities were followed.

q: Minimum number of Directors in one person company is/are:
e: A One Person Company needs at least one director under the Companies Act, 2013.

q:
Which of the following are consequences of Breach of Contract?
(A) Damages in ordinary course
(B) Remote damages and ordinary damages
(C) If stipulation by way of penalty is given in contract, then penalty is a consequence
(D) In quantifying damages, the inconvenience of non performance has to be considered
e: Sec. 73 gives ordinary damages (not remote damages) and counts inconvenience from non-performance; Sec. 74 deals with stipulated penalty.

q: The doctrine of separation forms the basis of American constitutional structure. Which of the following provisions of U.S. Constitution exemplify the concept of separation of powers?
e: Articles I, II and III vest legislative, executive and judicial power in separate branches.

q: Which of the following is a guide to the International Court of Justice to decide disputes submitted to it by State parties?
o: Principles of engagement laid down by the permanent members of the United Nations Security Council
The general principles of Law recognised by civilised nations
Previous decisions of the International Court of Justice
e: Art. 38 of the ICJ Statute lists general principles of law recognised by civilised nations as a source for deciding disputes.

q: Which book of John Rawls was published in the year 1971?
o: Justice: What is the Right Thing to Do?
e: Rawls' A Theory of Justice appeared in 1971.

q: Which among the following statements is generally understood to mean the essence of the Estrada Doctrine?
o: Recognition of government is unnecessary once the state has been recognised
Recognition of government is an imperative for recognition of state
Recognition of government provides legality to a state
State is a legal person under international law only if recognised by the United Nations
e: The Estrada Doctrine (Mexico, 1930) rejects formal recognition of new governments once the State is recognised.

q: The functions of the National Commission for minorities is provided for under which section of the relevant statute?
e: Sec. 9 of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 sets out the Commission's functions.

q:
As per the Supreme Court of India in the Oleum Gas leak case, the nature of duty owed by an enterprise engaged in hazardous industry posing a potential threat to health and safety of persons residing in the surrounding area is:
(A) Inherent duty
(B) Imperative and non-derogable duty
(C) Absolute and delegable duty
(D) Resolute duty
(E) Absolute and non-delegable duty
e: In M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak) the Court held such an enterprise owes an absolute and non-delegable duty to the community.

q:
What all items are included in the definition of biological resources according to the Biological Diversity Amendment Act, 2023?
(A) Plants and Animals
(B) Microorganisms or parts of their genetic material
(C) Human genetic material
(D) Plants, animals, microorganism or part of the derivatives including their value added products
e: Biological resources cover plants, animals and micro-organisms and their genetic material; human genetic material is excluded and value-added products are not part of the definition.

q: In Canada which document outlines the division of power between the Federal and Provincial governments?
e: Sections 91 and 92 of the British North America Act, 1867 divide powers between the Dominion and the provinces.

q: Which one of the following is not a ground of Fasid Marriages under Sunni Law?
o: Marriage in violation of Conditions of Fosterage
e: A marriage within prohibited fosterage is void (batil), not merely irregular (fasid); the other three are fasid grounds.

q: The word 'jurisprudence' owes its origin from the term 'jurisprudentia', which is given by:
e: 'Jurisprudentia' is a Latin (Roman) term meaning knowledge or skill in law.

q:
Which of the following acts are exempted from criminal liability under the Indian Penal Code?
(A) Act likely to cause harm done without criminal intent to prevent other harm
(B) Act causing slight harm
(C) Act of a child above 7 and under 12 years, but of immature understanding
(D) Act likely to cause harm done with criminal intent
e: Secs. 81 (necessity without criminal intent), 95 (slight harm) and 83 (child 7-12 of immature understanding) are exceptions; harm done with criminal intent is not.

q: In which of the following case victims/wife of bigamous marriage were allowed to get maintenance under Section 125 of Criminal Procedure Code?
o: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
Badshah v. Sou. Urmila Badshah Godse
e: Badshah v. Urmila Badshah Godse (2013) held that the second wife who married in ignorance of the first marriage can claim maintenance under Sec. 125.

q:
Which of the following are true for adjudicating officers under the Information Technology Act, 2000?
(A) Has the powers of Civil Court which are conferred on the Appellate Tribunal
(B) All proceedings before it deemed to be judicial proceedings U/ss 193 and 228 of IPC
(C) Deemed to be a Civil Court for purpose of order XXI of CPC, 1908
(D) Deemed to be a Civil Court for the purpose of Sections 340 and 341 of CrPC, 1973
e: Sec. 46(5) gives the adjudicating officer civil-court powers, treats proceedings as judicial under IPC 193 and 228, and treats it as a civil court for Order XXI CPC; the CrPC reference is to Secs. 345 and 346, not 340-341.

q: In which case, did the Supreme Court hold that Passive Euthanasia can be allowed under exceptional circumstances under strict monitoring of the Court?
o: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug v. Union of India
Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
P. Rathinam v. Union of India
e: Aruna Shanbaug (2011) permitted passive euthanasia in exceptional cases under court supervision.

q:
Arrange the following punishments in chronological order of which offenders are liable under Section 53 of IPC, 1860.
(A) Fine
(B) Forfeiture of property
(C) Imprisonment for Life
(D) Death
e: Sec. 53 lists punishments in order: death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment, forfeiture of property, fine.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (statute): (A) Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia; (B) Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda; (C) Statute of the International Criminal Court; (D) Statute of the Special Court for Sierra Leone
List II (Year): (I) 1998; (II) 2002; (III) 1994; (IV) 1993
e: ICTY 1993, ICTR 1994, ICC (Rome Statute) 1998, Special Court for Sierra Leone 2002.

q: The chairperson of The National Green Tribunal shall be appointed by whom?
o: Central Government in Consultation with The Chief Justice of India
Central Government in Consultation with The outgoing Chairperson of The Tribunal
Central Government in Consultation with President and Chief Justice of India
e: Under Sec. 4 of the NGT Act the Chairperson is appointed by the Central Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of India.

q: The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 has been repealed and replaced by which of the following Act?
e: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the 1986 Act.

q:
Arrange the following cases in their chronological order.

e: Voting Procedure (1955), Namibia (1971), Fisheries Jurisdiction (1974), Western Sahara (1975), Texaco v. Libya (1977).

q:
The fundamental rights under Indian Constitution are grouped under various heads. Mention which of the groups mentioned below is not adequately placed as per the articles.
(A) Right to Equality (Art 14-18)
(B) Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32-35A)
(C) Right to Freedom of Religion (Art 25-28)
(D) Right to Freedom (Art 19-21A)
(E) Right Against Exploitation (Art 23-24)
e: Right to Constitutional Remedies is Art. 32 and the Right to Freedom spans Arts. 19-22, so (B) and (D) are misplaced.

q:
Arrange the following provisions of Trade Marks Act, 1999 in its correct order as appearing in the Act pertaining to trademark registration process?
(A) Relative grounds of refusal
(B) Withdrawal of acceptance
(C) Opposition to register
(D) Absolute grounds
(E) Honest concurrent use
e: Sec. 9 (absolute grounds), Sec. 11 (relative grounds), Sec. 12 (honest concurrent use), Sec. 19 (withdrawal of acceptance), Sec. 21 (opposition).

List II (Theme): (I) Safeguard interest of working women; (II) Enforcement of rights under International Conventions; (III) Employment of Children in Construction Work; (IV) Rights of refugee
e: NHRC v. Arunachal Pradesh concerned Chakma refugees, Vishaka protected working women, and PUDR (Asiad workers) dealt with children employed in construction work.

q: What is the effect of acceptance of offer in the context of formation of contract?
o: A contract is created only after an offer is accepted
A contract is created only after an offer is rejected
A contract is not created after an offer is accepted
A contract is created only after an offer is revoked

Arrange the following rules in chronological order made under the Environment Protection Act, 1986.

(D) The Batteries (Management and Handling) Rules

e: Hazardous Chemical Rules (1989), Chemical Accidents Rules (1996), Batteries Rules (2001), C&D Waste Rules (2016), Wetlands Rules (2017).

q: Which of the following state is NOT included in Part XXI: Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions, of the India Constitution?
e: Part XXI has special provisions for Nagaland (371A), Assam (371B) and Telangana/Andhra Pradesh (371D-E), but none for Haryana.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (General Provisions Relating to State Responsibility as provided in Geneva Convention): (A) Geneva Convention I; (B) Geneva Convention II; (C) Geneva Convention III; (D) Geneva Convention IV
List II (Corresponding Articles): (I) Article 49-54; (II) Article 50-53; (III) Article 129-132; (IV) Article 146-149
e: The common provisions on repression of breaches are GC I Arts. 49-54, GC II Arts. 50-53, GC III Arts. 129-132 and GC IV Arts. 146-149.

q: Which of the following international treaty deal with access to published works for visually impaired and print disabled people?
e: The Marrakesh Treaty (2013) facilitates access to published works for blind, visually impaired and print-disabled persons.

q:
Which of the following does not correctly describe the nature of administrative law?
(A) In administrative law, emphasis is mainly laid on the study of the process of office action.
(B) Administrative law deals with the relation of individuals with organised power.
(C) Administrative law does not include any control mechanism against arbitrariness.
(D) In administrative law the balance of powers is seldom addressed independently.
e: Administrative law centres on procedure and the individual's relation with power, and it includes controls against arbitrariness and addresses reconciling power with liberty; (C) and (D) misdescribe it.

q:
Arrange the following provisions related to 'void agreement' in chronological order, as provided under the Indian Contract Act.
(A) Agreement in restraint of marriage
(B) Agreement in restraint of legal proceedings
(C) Agreement in restraint of trade
(D) Agreement without consideration
(E) Agreement which is ambiguous and uncertain
e: Sec. 25 (without consideration), 26 (restraint of marriage), 27 (restraint of trade), 28 (restraint of legal proceedings), 29 (uncertain agreements).

q:

List II (Sections under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881): (I) Section 9; (II) Section 5; (III) Section 138; (IV) Section 4

q: 'Hazardous Substance' is defined under which of the following Act?
o: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974

q:

e: Early childhood care is Art. 45, SC/ST interests Art. 46, free and compulsory education Art. 21A, and special provisions for economically weaker sections Art. 15(6).

q: Who amongst the below mentioned, has the power to make provisions of preparation of electoral rolls, delimitation of constituencies, with respect to elections to State Legislatures?
o: Governor, in consultation with the Chief Minister of respective State
e: Under Art. 327 Parliament may by law make provision for electoral rolls and delimitation of constituencies for State Legislatures.

q: For what purpose wednesbury test is applied?
o: To determine irrationality of administrative action
To determine proportionality of administrative action
To determine procedural impropriety of administrative action
To determine abuse of jurisdiction of administrative action
e: The Wednesbury test asks whether a decision is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have made it, i.e. irrationality.

List II (Provision on Penalties): (I) Section 15; (II) Section 3 A and 3 B; (III) Section 26; (IV) Section 51
e: Penalties: Forest (Conservation) Act Secs. 3A-3B, Wild Life Protection Act Sec. 51, Environment (Protection) Act Sec. 15, NGT Act Sec. 26.

q: Which of the following declaration of the Hague Convention Concerning Expanding Bullets of 1899 prohibits the use of dum-dum bullets?
e: The 1899 Hague Declaration (III) concerns expanding (dum-dum) bullets.

q: The word 'Secular' was added by which of the following amendments in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'integrity' in the Preamble.

q: In which of the following case it was held that "an agreement by a minor is void"?
o: Damodara Mudaliar v. Secretary of State for India
e: Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose (1903, Privy Council) held that a minor's agreement is void ab initio.

q: Which of the Article of the United Nations Charter sets out the principles on which the United Nation is based?
e: Article 2 of the UN Charter states the principles; Article 1 states the purposes.

q:

Arrange the following cases related to Indian Contract Act in chronological order (ascending):
(A) State of Madhya Pradesh v. Gobardhan Dass
(B) New India Assurance Co. v. Haryana Roadways, Sonipat
(C) Chairman-cum-M.D. T.N. Tea Plantation Corp. Ltd v. M/s Srinivasa Timbers
(D) G.S.R.T.C. v. B. Arunchandra & Co.
e: Answer follows the published key (A, B, C, D); the decision dates could not be independently verified.

q:
Arrange the following in order of their enactment (ascending):
(A) West German Constitution
(B) British North America Act
(C) Australian Constitution Act
(D) Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union
e: Articles of Confederation (1781), BNA Act (1867), Australian Constitution Act (1900), West German Basic Law (1949).

q: Which of the following is not a theory of legal personality?
e: Fiction, concession and bracket (symbolist) theories explain legal personality; the interest theory (Ihering) is a theory of the nature of rights.

q: On which date did the United Nations Organisation come into existence?
e: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 (UN Day) after ratification by the permanent members and a majority of signatories.

q: What is the US equivalent legislation of the Indian Right to Information Act, 2005?
e: Published key gives 1967. The FOIA was signed on 4 July 1966 and took effect a year later in 1967, so both years appear in sources.

q:
Arrange the following as per the correct order in the Indian Constitution (Article-wise):
(A) Establishment and Constitution of Supreme Court
(B) Original jurisdiction of Supreme Court
(C) Legislative power of Governor
(D) Transfer of a judge from one High Court to another
(E) Jurisdiction of existing High Courts
e: Art. 124, Art. 131, Art. 213 (Governor's power to legislate by ordinance), Art. 222 and Art. 225.

q: Which of the following UN organs addresses global justice concerns?
e: The ICJ is the UN's principal judicial organ and settles legal disputes between states.

q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India hold that telephone tapping is a serious invasion of an individual's right to privacy?
o: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India
R. Rajagopal v. State of T.N.
State of Maharashtra v. Madhukar Narain
e: PUCL v. Union of India (1997) held phone tapping violates privacy under Art. 21 unless done by procedure established by law, and laid down safeguards.

q:
Which of the following rules are related with 'nulla poena sine lege'?
(A) Retroactivity of Penal Laws
(B) Strict Construction
(C) Certainty in Legislation
(D) Accessibility of the law
(E) Liberal Interpretation
e: The maxim demands strict construction, certainty and accessibility of penal law; liberal interpretation runs against it. Non-retroactivity is also a facet, but option D is the best fit offered.

q: Seven Legislations are listed under Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. Which of the following Acts is not included under Schedule I?
o: The Scheduled Tribes and other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006
e: Schedule I covers the Water Act 1974, Water Cess Act 1977, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Air Act 1981, EPA 1986, Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 and Biological Diversity Act 2002.

q: Which of the following is not an absolute privilege under the law of torts?
o: Words written or spoken before a Tribunal
Communication relating to State matters made by one minister to another
e: Communication in self-protection is only a qualified privilege, defeated by malice; the others are absolute.

q: Who is the writer of the book titled 'The Post Modern Condition: A Report on Knowledge'?
e: The Postmodern Condition (1979) is by Jean-Francois Lyotard.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Jurist): (A) Montesquieu; (B) Lee; (C) Rudolph and Schlesinger; (D) Maine
List II (Statement/Opinion): (I) Comparative Constitution is strange; (II) Used the term Rechtsvergleichung; (III) Published Ancient Law in 1861; (IV) Father of Comparative Law
e: Maine's Ancient Law appeared in 1861 and Montesquieu is regarded as the father of comparative law; the other pairs follow the published key.

q: H and W are married. H filed a petition for divorce that was granted in his favour by the family court. When can H not remarry?
o: When there is no right of appeal against the decree
When the time for appeal has expired
When an appeal filed was dismissed
When the divorce decree was stayed
e: Under s.15 HMA remarriage is allowed once no appeal lies, the appeal period has expired or the appeal is dismissed; while the decree is stayed it is not final.

q:
Arrange the following cases on Gift under Muslim Law in chronological order (ascending):
(A) Maqbool Alam v. Khodaija
(B) Khurshida Begum v. Mohammad Farooq
(C) Abdul Rahim v. Abdul Zabar
(D) Valie v. Puthakkalam
e: Valia Peedikakkandi Katheesa Umma (1964) and Maqbool Alam (1966) come first, then Abdul Rahim v. Abdul Zabar (2009); the key places Khurshida Begum last (date not verified).

q:
Which of the following is not a general defence under Torts?
(A) Mistake
(B) Remoteness
(C) Necessity
(D) Consent
e: Mistake, necessity and consent are general defences; remoteness of damage limits liability but is not a defence.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Schedules under UCC of Uttarakhand, 2025): (A) Schedule 3; (B) Schedule 7; (C) Schedule 5; (D) Schedule 4
List II (Topic dealt under the Schedule): (I) form of probate; (II) form of certificate; (III) form of caveat; (IV) form of certificate and extended certificate
e: Answer follows the published key: Schedule 3 certificate, Schedule 4 caveat, Schedule 5 probate, Schedule 7 certificate and extended certificate (not independently verified).

q: From which country is Part IV of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
e: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

q:
Which of the following statements are not correct in respect of the US Constitution?
(A) Mode of Amendment is given in Article IV
(B) 2/3 of both houses can propose Amendments
(C) It has to be ratified by 3/4 of state legislatures
(D) Constitution cannot be amended by Convention
e: Amendment is governed by Article V, not IV (A wrong), and a convention called on application of 2/3 of the states can propose amendments (D wrong).
n: Statement (B) is garbled in the PDF ('% of both houses'); read as 2/3, consistent with the key.

q:
Arrange the following provisions of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 in the order of their appearance in the Act:
(A) Inquiry into complaints
(B) Procedure with respect to armed forces
(C) Investigation
(D) Powers relating to inquiry
(E) Statements made by person to the Commission
e: Sections: s.13 powers relating to inquiry, s.14 investigation, s.15 statements made to the Commission, s.17 inquiry into complaints, s.19 armed forces.

q: 'True subject matter of ownership in all cases is a right.' Who gave this statement?
e: Salmond treated ownership as the relation between a person and a right vested in him.

q:
Which of the following theory/theories is/are not closely connected to intellectual property rights?
(A) Economic Theory
(B) Autopoietic legal Theory
(C) Social Planning Theory
(D) Instrumentalist Theory
(E) Social Contract Theory
e: Economic, social planning, instrumentalist and social-contract (labour/natural rights) arguments are used to justify IP; autopoietic theory is a systems theory of law, not an IP theory.

q:
Which of the following statements are correct in the context of standard form contracts?
(A) Notice should not be contemporaneous with the consent.
(B) There should be a reasonable notice of the contractual terms.
(C) There should be no misrepresentation.
(D) The parties are not bound if the terms are contained in a contractual document.
(E) The contract with standard terms may be drafted by one party and on the same terms contracts may be made with numerous persons.
e: Notice must be reasonable and contemporaneous with consent, there must be no misrepresentation, and standard terms are drafted by one party for many contracts. Parties are bound by terms in a signed document.

q:
Arrange chronologically the following negotiations of GATT between 1947 to 1994 which led to the formation of WTO:
(A) Annecy
(B) Kennedy Round
(C) Tokyo
(D) Torquay
e: Annecy (1949), Torquay (1950-51), Kennedy Round (1964-67), Tokyo Round (1973-79).

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Profounder): (A) Mimansa; (B) Smriti; (C) Post Reformation Europe; (D) Korkunov
List II (Idea): (I) Law and Morals are same; (II) 'Idea of Values' is the foundation; (III) Law derives authority from State and not morals; (IV) There is distinction between obligatory and recommendatory rules
e: Mimansa separates obligatory and recommendatory rules, Smriti merges law and morals, post-Reformation Europe rooted law's authority in the State, and Korkunov rested law on the idea of values.

q:
Which of the following are correct about 'Rule of Law'?
(A) It is derived from French phrase 'La principe de legalite'
(B) It is called supremacy of law
(C) It promotes arbitrary governance
(D) Decisions could be made by discretion only
e: Rule of law (from the French principe de legalite) means supremacy of law and is the opposite of arbitrary or purely discretionary power.

q:
Arrange the following provisions in the correct order of their appearance in the Information Technology Act, 2000 (section-wise):
(A) Penalty for misrepresentation
(B) Punishment for identity theft
(C) Punishment for cyber terrorism
(D) Penalty for breach of confidentiality and privacy
(E) Punishment for violation of privacy
e: s.66C identity theft, s.66E violation of privacy, s.66F cyber terrorism, s.71 misrepresentation, s.72 breach of confidentiality and privacy.

q:
Which of the following are correct about 'legal theory'?
(A) It defines Law
(B) It analyses legal concepts
(C) It deals with mere theory and has no practical importance
(D) It highlights salient features of legal system
e: Legal theory defines law, analyses concepts and exposes features of legal systems; it has practical importance, so C is wrong.

q:
What are the duties of a bailee as provided under the Indian Contract Act?
(A) Duty to take reasonable care of the goods bailed.
(B) Duty not to make unauthorized use of the goods.
(C) Duty not to mix bailor's goods with his own goods.
(D) Duty to return the goods on fulfilment of the purpose.
(E) Duty not to deliver to the bailor increase or profit on the goods bailed.
e: A bailee must take care (s.151), not misuse (s.154), not mix goods (s.155) and return them (s.160); he must deliver any increase or profit to the bailor (s.163), so E is wrong.

q: Which of the following cases does not relate to the concept of absolute liability under law of India?
o: Indian Council for Enviro-legal Action v. Union of India
Klaus Mittelbachert v. East India Hotels of India
Madras Railway Co. v. Zamindar of Carvatenagaram
M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
e: Madras Railway Co. v. Zamindar of Carvatenagaram applied the Rylands v. Fletcher rule of strict liability; absolute liability is the M.C. Mehta line of cases.

q: 'International law is the body of rules and principles of action which are binding upon civilised states in their relations with one another.' This definition is attributed to whom of the following?
e: This is J.L. Brierly's definition of international law.

q:
Which of the following is not true in the context of powers of the President in the Indian Constitution?
(A) The President is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces of the country.
(B) All treaties and international agreements are negotiated and concluded in the name of the President though subject to ratification by the Parliament.
(C) President has power to summon and prorogue the Parliament and can dissolve the Lok Sabha.
(D) President is empowered to promulgate ordinances during recess of Parliament under Article 213 of the Indian Constitution.
e: The President's ordinance power during recess is under Art. 123; Art. 213 is the Governor's ordinance power, so D is wrong.

q: Which of the following Canadian Legislation does not have provisions related to Federation?
e: There is no 'Law of Federation, 1802'; the BNA Act (now Constitution Act, 1867) created the federation and the Constitution Act, 1982 patriated the constitution.

q: Which of the following Articles is referred to as the heart and soul of the Indian Constitution?
e: Dr. Ambedkar described Art. 32 (right to constitutional remedies) as the heart and soul of the Constitution.

q:
Arrange the following provisions pertaining to procedure of granting patent (section-wise) in their correct sequence:
(A) Time for putting application in order for grant
(B) Request for examination
(C) Publication of application
(D) Priority date of claims of a complete specification
(E) Mention of inventor as such in patent
e: Patents Act, 1970: s.11 priority date, s.11A publication, s.11B request for examination, s.21 time for putting application in order, s.28 mention of inventor.

q: What does 'injury' mean under section 44 of IPC, 1860 and Section 2(14) of BNS, 2023?
o: Any harm illegally caused to a person in body and mind
Any harm illegally caused to a person in body and property
Any harm illegally caused to a person in body, mind, reputation or property
Any harm illegally caused to a person in body, mind and reputation
e: Injury means any harm illegally caused to any person in body, mind, reputation or property.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Maxim): (A) Erga Omnes; (B) Jus Cogens; (C) Pacta Sunt Servanda; (D) Rebus Sic Stantibus
List II (Meaning): (I) Relation to all; (II) Peremptory norm; (III) Agreements are to be respected; (IV) Essential circumstances remain unchanged
e: Erga omnes means owed to all, jus cogens a peremptory norm, pacta sunt servanda that agreements must be kept, and rebus sic stantibus that circumstances remain as they stand.
n: The answer key printed in the PDF is option D, (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV), which is factually wrong (e.g. erga omnes is not 'agreements are to be respected'). Option C is the only correct matching and is used here.

q:
In which of the following cases was the golden rule for framing a prospectus formulated by V.C. Kindersley?
(A) Methodist Church v. Union of India
(B) R. v. Registrar of Companies
(C) New Brunswick Canada Railway Co. v. Muggeridge
(D) Jubilee Cotton Mills Ltd. v. Lewis
e: Vice-Chancellor Kindersley in New Brunswick and Canada Railway Co. v. Muggeridge (1860) required a prospectus to disclose everything with perfect fairness and honesty.

q:
Arrange the following cases on Maintenance in their chronological order (ascending):
(A) Saira Banu v. A.M. Abdul Gafoor
(B) Danial Latifi v. Union of India
(C) Noor Saba Khatoon v. Mohd. Quasim
(D) Md. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
e: Shah Bano (1985) is first and Danial Latifi (2001) last, with Saira Banu and Noor Saba Khatoon (1997) in between.

q:
Which of the following are characteristics of 'Legal Right'?
(A) Rights are vested in person and not against a person
(B) Rights are act or omission in favour of person entitled
(C) Act or omission relates to a thing
(D) Every legal right has a title
e: Salmond's elements: person of inherence, person of incidence (the right is against a person, so A is wrong), content (act or omission), object and title.

q: Which of the following is a landmark case on the importance of 'nationality'?
e: Nottebohm (Liechtenstein v. Guatemala, ICJ 1955) required a genuine link between a state and its national for diplomatic protection.

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains special provisions for the administration and control of scheduled areas in several states?
e: The Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram (Sixth Schedule).

q: Which of the following is not true in the context of CSR?
o: CSR Committee should consist of only one Director
CSR provision was introduced by the Companies Act, 2013
Company should spend at least 2% of average net profits made during the immediately preceding 3 financial years
CSR is an implied agreement between the company and society to impart goods and services in some way advantageous to the society
e: Section 135 requires a CSR Committee of at least three directors (including an independent director), not one.

q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Doctrine of Legitimate Expectations?
(A) The doctrine has an important place in the development of law of judicial review.
(B) Doctrine is well established and operated in the domain of public law.
(C) Doctrine has been developed both in the context of reasonableness and natural justice.
(D) The concept of legitimate expectation made its first appearance in the case of Union of India v. Hindustan Development Corpn.
e: The doctrine (from Schmidt v. Secretary of State, 1969) is established in public law, judicial review, reasonableness and natural justice; it did not first appear in Hindustan Development Corp. (1993).

q: The power of judicial review was first adopted/applied by the Supreme Court of USA in which of the following cases?
e: Marbury v. Madison (1803) established judicial review in the United States.

q:
Which of the following is not a guardian under the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956?
(A) Guardian for Marriage
(B) Maternal Guardian
(C) Testamentary Guardian
(D) Guardian by Affinity
e: The Act recognises natural, testamentary and court-appointed guardians; per the published key only 'guardian for marriage' is not a recognised category.

q:
Arrange the following in the order in which they appear in the Indian Contract Act:
(A) Agreement by way of Wager
(B) Agreement in restraint of legal proceedings
(C) Agreement in restraint of trade
(D) Agreement of restraint of marriage
e: s.26 restraint of marriage, s.27 restraint of trade, s.28 restraint of legal proceedings, s.30 wager.

q:
Which of the following articles incorporate the expression 'right to life'?
(A) Article 3 of UDHR, 1948
(B) Article 6 of ICCPR, 1966
(C) Article 9 of ICESCR, 1966
(D) Article 3 of OP2 of ICCPR, 1989
e: UDHR Art. 3 and ICCPR Art. 6 expressly protect the right to life; ICESCR Art. 9 concerns social security and Art. 3 of OP2 is a procedural (reporting) provision.

q:
Arrange the following Conventions in the chronological order of their coming into force:
(A) The Biological Weapons Convention
(B) The Chemical Weapons Convention
(C) The Conventional Weapons Convention
(D) The Ottawa Convention on Anti-Personnel Mines
e: BWC 1975, CCW 1983, CWC 1997, Ottawa Convention 1999.

q: Which one of the following is an incorrect statement in the context of the characteristic features of a Waqf?
o: A Waqf once created cannot be revoked
A Waqf property vests in God
e: A testamentary waqf (made by will) is revocable like a will; an inter vivos waqf, once validly created, is irrevocable.

q: A Christian man X and a Hindu girl Y eloped and entered into an 'Agreement of Marriage' on ₹50 stamp paper and registered it at the Registrar office. They exchanged garlands and X tied a Mangalsutra around the neck of Y. Is it a valid marriage?
o: It is a valid marriage as it is registered by agreement
It is valid marriage as ceremonies are performed
It is not a valid marriage as legal validity test is not complete
It is a valid marriage as customary rites of the parties were followed
e: A marriage between a Christian and a Hindu is valid only if solemnised under the Special Marriage Act, 1954; a registered private agreement and Hindu rites satisfy no statute.

q: Which one of the following Reports of the Law Commission of India supported/recommended the inclusion of irretrievable breakdown of marriage as a ground for divorce?
e: The 71st Report (1978) recommended irretrievable breakdown of marriage as a ground for divorce.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Term/Doctrine): (A) Jus Necessitatis; (B) Malice; (C) Dolus and Culpa; (D) Intention and Negligence
List II (Opinion): (I) Collective term for intention and recklessness; (II) Two forms of Mens rea; (III) Two alternative conditions of Penal Liability; (IV) Right of the man to do from which he cannot be dissuaded
e: Jus necessitatis is the right to do what one cannot be dissuaded from; malice covers intention and recklessness; dolus and culpa are the two forms of mens rea; intention and negligence are alternative conditions of penal liability.

q:

e: Father's sister's son is a cognate, daughter's son's daughter a Class II heir, father's brother's daughter an agnate, and a predeceased son's daughter a Class I heir.

q: Which of the following provisions of the Partnership Act explains the evidentiary value of entries in the Register of Firms?
e: Section 68 deals with the evidentiary value of entries in the Register of Firms.

q: 'X', an insane person, kills 'Y' by firing from a loaded gun. 'X' has committed which of the following offences?
o: An offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder
e: An act done by a person who, through unsoundness of mind, cannot know its nature is no offence (s.84 IPC / s.22 BNS).

q:
Which of the following is true about Separation of Power in the Constitution of Canada?
(A) Separation exists between only Judiciary and Parliament
(B) Separation exists between executive and legislature
(C) There is no general separation of power
(D) Canadian Constitution has no parallel with Presidentialism
e: Per the published key: Canada has responsible government with executive and legislature fused, so there is no general separation of powers; only the judiciary is separated.

q: Which of the following is the guiding principle of genetics (inheritance) under Mitakshara?
e: Mitakshara's rule of inheritance rests on propinquity of blood relationship (sapinda), unlike Dayabhaga's spiritual efficacy.

q:

e: Wade: law on control of governmental power; Garner: rules recognised by courts regulating administration; Griffith & Street: operation and control of administrative authorities; Jennings: law relating to the administration.

q: Which of the following Amendments has inserted the theme 'Secularism, Socialism and Integrity' in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India give a split verdict on 23rd July, 2024 in a matter involving health, environment and intergenerational equity?
o: Animal Welfare Board of India v. U.O.I
e: A two-judge bench delivered a split verdict on GM mustard in Gene Campaign v. Union of India on 23 July 2024.

q:
Mark the incorrect statement as per Muslim Law on Wills.
(A) A will of a minor can be ratified by him on attaining majority.
(B) The will of a person of unsound mind cannot be ratified on attaining sanity.
(C) Will made by a sane person will become invalid if subsequently he becomes insane.
(D) A will made by a person who subsequently commits suicide is invalid.
e: Per the published key only D is incorrect: a will made before the suicidal act is not invalidated merely by the later suicide.

q: In which of the following cases did the apex court of India issue fourteen directions to the Union and State Governments to ensure complete eradication of manual scavenging and hazardous cleaning?
o: Govt. of NCT of Delhi v. U.O.I
Adivasis for Social and Human Rights Action v. U.O.I
e: In Dr. Balram Singh v. Union of India (2023) the Supreme Court issued 14 directions to eradicate manual scavenging and hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Type of IPR): (A) Geographical Indication; (B) Trademark; (C) Patent; (D) Copyright
List II (Concept): (I) Post grant opposition; (II) Protection of Rights Management Information (RMI); (III) Prohibition of Assignment; (IV) Honest Concurrent use
e: A GI cannot be assigned, trade marks allow honest concurrent use, patents have post-grant opposition, and copyright protects rights management information.

q: Which of the following provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 identifies shares and debentures as movable property?
e: Section 44 declares the shares or debentures of a member to be movable property transferable as provided by the articles.

q: Which of the following is not the meaning of the term 'dominant position' under the Competition Act, 2002?
o: Affect its competitors or consumers in its favour
e: The Explanation to s.4 defines dominant position as a position of strength enabling independence from competitive forces or the ability to affect competitors or consumers in one's favour; cartels fall under s.3.

q: Estrada doctrine dealing with recognition of States and Government is primarily related to which country?
e: The Estrada Doctrine (1930) is named after Mexican Foreign Secretary Genaro Estrada and rejects formal recognition of governments.

q:
Which of the following decisions are related to extradition?
(A) Savarkar case
(B) Abu Salem case
(C) Castioni, re case
(D) Meunier, re case
(E) Paquete Habana case
e: The Paquete Habana (US, 1900) concerned prize law and customary international law, not extradition.

q:

List II (Case laws): (I) Ferguson v. Wilson; (II) R.R. Kothandraman v. Commr. of Income Tax; (III) Great Eastern Rly. Co. v. Turner; (IV) Forest of Dean Coal Mining Co., Re
e: Ferguson v. Wilson (agents), Kothandraman (employee), Great Eastern Rly. v. Turner (trustees), Re Forest of Dean (fiduciary).

q:
Which of the following Theory/Theories is/are predominantly related to 'attempt' in law of crimes?
(A) Last seen theory
(B) Proximity theory
(C) Theory of Impossibility
(D) Reformatory Theory
e: Proximity and impossibility are the standard tests/theories for attempt; 'last seen' is an evidentiary doctrine and the reformatory theory concerns punishment.

q: When did the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notify the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024?
e: MoEFCC notified the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024 on 22 October 2024.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Section under the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019): (A) Section 164B; (B) Section 162; (C) Section 164A; (D) Section 159
List II (Provision): (I) Information to be given regarding accident; (II) Motor Vehicle Accident Fund; (III) Scheme for golden hour; (IV) Scheme for Interim relief for claimants
e: s.164B Motor Vehicle Accident Fund, s.162 golden hour scheme, s.164A interim relief scheme, s.159 information regarding accident.

q:
Arrange the following in the historical order of development of Natural Law theories (ascending):
(A) Union with Divine is end of law
(B) Church is the law giver
(C) Development of idea of Rationalism
(D) Revival of Natural Law
e: Early Christian thought (law as union with the divine), then medieval church authority, then rationalist natural law, then the 20th-century revival.

q:
Match List I with List II:

List II (Title of books): (I) International Humanitarian Law; (II) The Universalism of Human Rights; (III) Biopiracy: The Plunder of Nature & Knowledge; (IV) The Culturalisation of Human Right Law
e: Arnold edited The Universalism of Human Rights, Shiva wrote Biopiracy, Lenzerini wrote The Culturalisation of Human Rights Law, and Crawford & Pert wrote International Humanitarian Law.

q:
Match List I with List II:

List II (Exception number): (I) Exception 5; (II) Exception 1; (III) Exception 4; (IV) Exception 2
e: Exception 1 is grave and sudden provocation, Exception 2 exceeding private defence, Exception 4 sudden fight and Exception 5 consent.

q: The United States Ombudsman Association was founded in which year?
e: The USOA was founded in 1977.

q:
Which of the following statements are incorrect in the context of Adoption?
(A) Muslim Law does not recognise adoption.
(B) A married Hindu male can adopt a child without obtaining consent of his wife.
(C) Child must not have completed the age of fifteen years.
(D) Two persons cannot adopt the same child except in case of a husband and wife.
(E) A person who is a major and sound mind can only be adopted.
e: A married Hindu male needs his wife's consent (s.7 HAMA) and only a minor (normally under 15) can be adopted, so B and E are incorrect.

q:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Judicial decisions): (A) State of Gujarat v. Reliance Industries Ltd & Ors.; (B) Municipal Corporation Ghaziabad v. Central Pollution Control Board; (C) Hanuman Laxman Aroskar v. U.O.I; (D) Riddhima Pandey v. U.O.I

q:

q:
Which of the following statements are attributable to H. L. A. Hart’s concept of law?
(A) Primary rules confer powers, while secondary rules impose duties.
(B) Secondary rules enable lawmakers to modify legal rules in accordance with the needs of society.
(C) The validity of a law is tested by reference to the rule of recognition.
(D) Moral judgments can be established through rational argument, evidence or proof.
(E) A legal system must be concerned with both what the law is and what it ought to be.
e: Hart: secondary rules (recognition, change, adjudication) confer powers and primary rules impose duties, and validity is tested by the rule of recognition. So A is reversed, and D and E are not Hartian propositions.

Independently interpreting and resolving legal questions that are not expressly or conclusively addressed by the Qur’an.
Presuming the existence of a lawful union between the parents of an acknowledged child.

(E) Daimler Co. Ltd. v. Continental Tyre and Rubber Co.

Section 15 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988

Section 17 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988

e: Patents Act 1970, Trade Marks Act 1999, Geographical Indications Act 1999 (same year), Biological Diversity Act 2002.

e: Section 4 of the Patents Act, 1970 bars patents for inventions relating to atomic energy.

q: Which of the following doctrines holds that a State should continue diplomatic relations with other States without regard to revolutionary changes in their governments?
e: The Estrada Doctrine (Mexico, 1930) holds that relations should continue irrespective of revolutionary changes of government, without any act of recognition.

q: Under Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which of the following is not an essential element of a contingent contract?
o: There must be a valid contract to do or not to do something.
The performance of the contract must depend on the happening or non-happening of an uncertain event.
The uncertain event must be collateral to the contract.
The event must not be at the discretion of the promisor.
e: NTA dropped this question. Section 31 requires a contract, dependence on an uncertain event and that the event be collateral; the 'not at the promisor's discretion' point is a case-law gloss, not in the definition.
n: NTA dropped this question. In the original paper option C read 'non-necessarily collateral' (the odd one out); this version says 'must be collateral', which makes every option look essential.

q: Article 2 of the Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, 1951, deals with:
o: The general obligations of Contracting States towards refugees
The general obligations of refugees towards the country in which they find themselves
e: Article 2 of the 1951 Refugee Convention states the duties of refugees towards the country in which they find themselves (Art. 3 is non-discrimination; Art. 33 non-refoulement).

q:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order, from earliest to latest:
(A) Anti-Hijacking Act
(B) Diplomatic Relations (Vienna Convention) Act
(C) Anti-Apartheid (United Nations Convention) Act
(D) Genocide Convention
e: Genocide Convention 1948, Diplomatic Relations (Vienna Convention) Act 1972, Anti-Apartheid (UN Convention) Act 1981, Anti-Hijacking Act 1982.

Match List I with List II.

List II (Subject Matter): (I) Viva voce test; (II) Transgender rights; (III) Special courts for speedier trials; (IV) Right to know
e: Anwar Ali Sarkar concerned special courts for speedier trial, Ashok Kumar Yadav the viva voce test, NALSA transgender rights and Dinesh Trivedi the right to know.

q: The legal maxim in pari delicto means:
o: A person of unsound mind has no will.
An act done by me against my will.
e: In pari delicto means 'in equal fault'.

q:
“Tortious liability arises from the breach of a duty primarily fixed by law. This duty is owed to persons generally, and its breach is redressible by an action for unliquidated damages.”
This definition is attributable to which of the following jurists?
e: This is Winfield's definition of tortious liability.

q: Which of the following formulations does not incorporate Professor A. V. Dicey’s concept of the Rule of Law?
o: Absence or excess of discretionary power
e: Dicey's rule of law excludes arbitrary power or wide discretionary authority and stresses equality before law and the predominance of the legal spirit. 'Absence or excess of discretionary power' is not his formulation.

q:
Arrange the following offences against the State under the Indian Penal Code, 1860, in ascending order of their section numbers:

(B) Waging, or attempting to wage, war against the Government of India
(C) A public servant voluntarily allowing a prisoner of State or war to escape
(D) Waging war against an Asiatic power in alliance with the Government of India
e: Sections: 121 (waging war), 124A (sedition), 125 (war against Asiatic power in alliance with India), 128 (public servant allowing prisoner of State to escape).

q:
Arrange the following chapters of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, in the order in which they appear in the Act, from earliest to latest:

(B) Chapter on Offences Against Women and Children
(C) Chapter on Offences Affecting the Human Body
(D) Chapter on Punishments
(E) Chapter on Offences Against Property
e: BNS order: Ch. II Punishments, Ch. III General Exceptions, Ch. V Offences against Woman and Child, Ch. VI Offences Affecting the Human Body, Ch. XVII Offences against Property.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
(A) The NHRC may visit any jail or other institution under the control of the State Government without informing the State Government.
(B) The NHRC may undertake and promote research in the field of human rights.
(C) The NHRC cannot intervene in any proceeding relating to a violation of human rights.
(D) The NHRC may review factors, including acts of terrorism, that inhibit the enjoyment of human rights.
(E) The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter that is pending before a State Commission or any other commission duly constituted under any law.
e: NTA's key is option D. B (s.12(h)) and D (s.12(e)) are correct, but s.12(c) requires intimation to the State Government for jail visits, so A looks wrong and E (s.36) looks right. The key is debatable.

q:
Consider the following statements concerning the right to education under Article 26 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948:
(A) Elementary education shall be optional.
(B) Technical and professional education shall be made generally available.
(C) Education shall be free, at least at the elementary and fundamental stages.
(D) Higher education shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit.
(E) Elementary education shall be compulsory.
e: Art. 26 UDHR: education free at least at elementary and fundamental stages, elementary education compulsory, technical and professional education generally available, higher education equally accessible on merit.

q:
Match List I with List II.

List II (Provisions): (I) Section 148 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; (II) Section 124 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; (III) Section 126 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; (IV) Section 182 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872
e: Agent and principal: s.182; bailment: s.148; indemnity: s.124; guarantee: s.126 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

q:
The Marrakesh Treaty, which facilitates access to published works for persons who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise print-disabled, has the following objectives or features:
(A) It seeks to provide access to published works for visually impaired persons.
(B) India was the first country to ratify the Treaty.
(C) The Treaty does not provide for cross-border sharing of accessible-format copies.
(D) It seeks to facilitate the adoption of domestic copyright exceptions by countries that ratify it.
e: The Marrakesh Treaty (2013) aims to improve access for the print-disabled, requires domestic copyright exceptions and allows cross-border exchange of accessible copies (so C is wrong); India was the first to ratify.

q:
“The full participation of women is essential to achieve sustainable development, and women have a vital role in environmental management and development.”
This principle is set out in which of the following principles of the Rio Declaration on Environment and Development, 1992?
e: Principle 20 of the Rio Declaration recognises women's vital role in environmental management and development.

q:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Cases): (A) Temple of Preah Vihear; (B) Mavrommatis Palestine Concessions; (C) R. v. Keyn; (D) Diversion of Water from the Meuse
List II (Principles): (I) Justice, equity and good conscience; (II) Principle of estoppel; (III) Res judicata; (IV) Principle of subrogation
e: Preah Vihar is the estoppel/acquiescence case (II). NTA's key is option A for the remaining pairings; this is one of the less certain matches.

q:
Arrange the following international organisations in chronological order of their establishment, from earliest to latest:
(A) International Telecommunication Union
(B) World Intellectual Property Organization
(C) International Finance Corporation
(D) International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
(E) Food and Agriculture Organization
e: Actual order is ITU (1865), IBRD (1944), FAO (1945), IFC (1956), WIPO (1967). NTA's key retains option B, which gets only the ending right.
n: No option gives the correct order (A, D, E, C, B), and option D repeats B. NTA's final key retains option B.

q: Which of the following jurists defined jurisprudence as the “science of the first principles of civil law”?
e: Salmond defined jurisprudence as the 'science of the first principles of the civil law'.

q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court hold that not all live-in relationships are relationships “in the nature of marriage,” and discuss circumstances in which such a relationship may or may not exist?
o: Indra Sarma v. V. K. V. Sarma
Lata Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
e: In Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013) the Supreme Court held that not every live-in relationship is 'in the nature of marriage' and listed the relevant factors.

q: Under Section 2(1)(d) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, which of the following is not included in the definition of “body corporate”?
o: A company as defined under Section 2(20) of the Companies Act, 2013
A limited liability partnership incorporated outside India
e: NTA dropped this question. Under s.2(1)(d) of the LLP Act, 'body corporate' excludes a corporation sole and co-operative societies.
n: NTA dropped this question. The original paper cited 'Section 2(8)' of the LLP Act instead of 2(1)(d).

q:
A purchases a horse from B. A intends to use the horse for riding but does not disclose this purpose to B. The horse is unsuitable for riding but is suitable for being driven in a carriage. Consider the following statements:
(A) A can return the horse under the implied condition as to fitness for a particular purpose under Section 16 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930.
(B) A can neither reject the horse nor claim compensation from B.
(C) The situation is covered by the rule expressed in the maxim caveat emptor.
(D) The situation falls within the exception under Section 16(1), which deals with implied conditions as to the fitness of goods for a particular purpose.
e: Section 16(1) implied fitness applies only if the buyer makes the purpose known. A did not, and the horse is fit for carriage use, so caveat emptor applies and A has no remedy.

q:
Which of the following marks may be registered under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, in India?
(A) The shape of a light bulb, where the shape makes the bulb more energy-efficient.
(B) The term “Icy Freeze” for ice cream.
(C) The term “Semiclo” for a food processor.
(D) The term “Matokla” for coffee.
e: NTA dropped this question. A functional shape (s.9(3)) and the descriptive 'Icy Freeze' are not registrable, while coined marks like 'Semiclo' and 'Matokla' are.
n: NTA dropped this question. The original paper cited the 'Trademark Act, 1989' instead of the 1999 Act.

q: Which of the following cases distinguishes between an offer and an invitation to receive offers?
o: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. (1893)
e: Harvey v. Facey (1893) held that a price quotation is a mere invitation to offer, not an offer.

q:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the effect of the dissolution of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) on business pending before Parliament?
(A) A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses.
(B) A contempt proceeding pending in the House lapses.
(C) A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha does not lapse.
(D) A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha that has not been passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse.
(E) A Bill passed by both Houses but pending the President’s assent does not lapse.
e: Under Art. 107, a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha (or passed by it but pending in the Rajya Sabha) lapses; a Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, or awaiting assent after passage by both Houses, does not.

q:
Consider the following statements concerning the right to education under the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR):
(A) Primary education shall be optional and free for all.
(B) Secondary education, in its different forms, shall be made generally available and accessible to all.
(C) Fundamental education shall be encouraged or intensified for persons who have not received or completed the whole period of primary education.
(D) The material conditions of teaching staff shall be continuously improved.
(E) The right to education shall promote scientific progress, fellowship and affirmative-action programmes.
e: NTA dropped this question. Art. 13 ICESCR makes primary education compulsory and free (A wrong) and covers secondary, fundamental education and teachers' conditions (B, C, D); E is not in Art. 13.
n: NTA dropped this question. The original paper cited 'ICCPR under Article 13(2) of ICCPR, 1996'; the relevant treaty is the ICESCR.

q: The system of droit administrative evolved in which of the following jurisdictions?
e: Droit administratif developed in France, with the Conseil d'État at its apex.

q:
Arrange the following treaties and conventions in chronological order, from earliest to latest:

(B) Brussels Convention Relating to the Distribution of Programme-Carrying Signals Transmitted by Satellite
(C) Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms for the Purposes of Patent Procedure

e: Rome Convention 1961, Brussels Satellite Convention 1974, Budapest Treaty 1977, Trademark Law Treaty 1994.

q:
Match List I with List II.
List I (General Exceptions): (A) An act of a child under seven years of age; (B) An act likely to cause harm, done without criminal intent to prevent other harm; (C) Mistake of fact; (D) An act by a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication administered against their will
List II (Sections of the Indian Penal Code): (I) Section 76; (II) Section 85; (III) Section 82; (IV) Section 81
e: Child under seven: s.82; harm without criminal intent to prevent other harm: s.81; mistake of fact: s.76; involuntary intoxication: s.85 IPC.

q:
Which of the following statements are attributable to the interest theory of legal rights?
(A) A right is an interest protected by law.
(B) A right is based on the sovereign power of the State.
(C) A subjective right is a metaphysical abstraction.
(D) A legal right is a legally protected interest.
(E) The main object of law is to protect human interests and prevent conflicts between individual interests.
e: The interest theory (Ihering, Pound) treats a legal right as a legally protected interest and law's aim as protecting interests and reconciling conflicts. NTA's key is option C.
n: In the original paper statement A read 'A right is an interest defined of the former will' (the will theory); this version rewrites it as an interest-theory statement, which would make A, D and E all valid. The key (option C) follows the original wording.

q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court hold that the “width of power test” or the “direct impact and effect test” should be used to determine whether a constitutional amendment violates the basic structure of the Constitution?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008)
Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015)
e: NTA's key identifies the 2015 Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (NJAC) decision as applying the 'width of power' / 'direct impact and effect' test.

q: With regard to defamation, which of the following statements is not correct?
o: Under English criminal law, only libel has traditionally been recognised as an offence.
Under English tort law, slander is actionable per se in every case.
In India, criminal law does not distinguish between libel and slander.
Libel is generally associated with written or otherwise permanent publication, whereas slander is generally associated with spoken or otherwise transient publication.
e: Slander is actionable only on proof of special damage, apart from exceptions such as imputations of crime or unchastity; it is not actionable per se in every case.

q:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Cases): (A) Lalman Shukla v. Gauri Dutt; (B) Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.; (C) Hadley v. Baxendale; (D) Phillips v. Brooks
List II (Legal Principles or Provisions): (I) Section 30 — Wagering agreements; (II) Section 20 — Mistake of fact; (III) Section 4 — Communication when complete; (IV) Section 73 — Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
e: Lalman Shukla: s.4; Carlill: s.30 (wagering argument); Hadley v. Baxendale: s.73; Phillips v. Brooks: s.20 (mistake).

q: Which provision of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 empowers a State Government, after consultation with or on the recommendation of the State Board, to declare an area within the State a water pollution prevention and control area?
e: Section 19 of the Water Act, 1974 lets the State Government, after consulting the State Board, restrict the Act's application to specified areas.

q:
Consider the following statements concerning the powers of the General Assembly under the Charter of the United Nations:
(A) Resolutions or declarations of the General Assembly are generally recommendatory and are not binding on Member States in the same way as binding treaty obligations.
(B) Under Article 2(7) of the UN Charter, the General Assembly may intervene in matters that are essentially within the domestic jurisdiction of States.
(C) The General Assembly may make recommendations to promote international cooperation in the political field.
(D) The General Assembly may promote the progressive development of international law and its codification.
(E) The General Assembly may make recommendations to promote international cooperation in the economic, social, cultural, educational and health fields.
e: General Assembly resolutions are recommendatory (A); it may make recommendations on political, legal-codification and economic, social, cultural, educational and health cooperation (C, D, E). Art. 2(7) bars intervention in domestic matters (B wrong).

q: Which of the following is not a ground for opposition to the grant of a patent under the Patents Act, 1970?
o: The invention, insofar as claimed in any claim of the complete specification, was published before the priority date of that claim.
The complete specification fails to disclose the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention.
The subject matter of a claim in the complete specification does not constitute an invention within the meaning of the Patents Act, 1970.
The applicant for the patent wrongfully obtained the invention.
e: NTA's key marks option B. Section 25 does list failure to disclose or wrong mention of the source of biological material among opposition grounds, so the key is debatable.

Arrange the following decisions of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), delivered in its contentious jurisdiction, in chronological order, from earliest to latest:

(B) Corfu Channel Case
(C) Asylum (Colombia v. Peru) Case
(D) Minquiers and Ecrehos (France v. United Kingdom) Case
e: Corfu Channel (1949), Asylum (1950), Anglo-Norwegian Fisheries (1951), Minquiers and Ecrehos (1953).

“You must take reasonable care to avoid acts or omissions that you can reasonably foresee would be likely to injure your neighbour.”
This statement is attributed to which of the following?
o: Lord Derby in Campbell v. Paddington
Blackburn J. in Rylands v. Fletcher
Lord Macmillan in Heaven v. Pender
Lord Atkin in Donoghue v. Stevenson
e: Lord Atkin's neighbour principle in Donoghue v. Stevenson (1932).

q:
According to Hohfeld’s analysis of legal rights and their correlatives, which of the following statements are correct?
(A) The correlative of liberty is no-right.
(B) The correlative of immunity is power.
(C) The correlative of disability is immunity.
(D) The correlative of power is liability.
(E) The contradictory of immunity is the absence of power in another.
e: NTA dropped this question. Liberty-no-right, power-liability and disability-immunity are correlatives; immunity's correlative is disability, so B is wrong and E confuses correlatives with contradictories. Option A is the closest fit.
n: NTA dropped this question. Statement E is garbled, and no option lists exactly A, C and D.

q: Under which constitutional provision was Parliament empowered to enact the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981?
e: The Air Act, 1981 was enacted under Art. 253 to implement the decisions of the 1972 Stockholm Conference.

List II (Cases): (I) Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration; (II) Charles Gurmukh Sobhraj v. Delhi Administration; (III) Attorney General of India v. Lakhma Devi; (IV) T. V. Vatheeswaran v. State of Tamil Nadu
