List II (Year of enactment): (I) 1956; (II) 1986; (III) 1984; (IV) 1995
e: Wakf Act 1995, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956, Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986, Family Courts Act 1984.

q: During an emergency, Parliament may authorise a lump-sum grant without specifying the particular objects to which the money will be applied. Under Article 116(1)(b) of the Constitution, this is known as which of the following?
e: A vote of credit under Art. 116(1)(b) is a lump-sum grant for unforeseen demands where details cannot be specified.

q: Which of the following situations is valid under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956?
o: Anil, a Hindu male, adopted Sunny, aged 10, in 1986. A son, Sunil, was born to Anil’s wife in 1987. In 1988, Anil cancelled Sunny’s adoption and informed him that he was no longer to be regarded as his son.
Albert, a citizen of the United States of America, adopts an abandoned child who is being brought up in an orphanage in India.
Kamini, a 23-year-old Hindu widow, adopts her brother’s daughter, who is two and a half years old.
Kamla, who had been living separately from her husband for six years, adopts a three-year-old girl.
e: Kamini, a major Hindu widow, can adopt. An adoption cannot be cancelled (s.15), the adopter must be Hindu, and a married woman can adopt only if her husband is dead, has renounced the world or been declared of unsound mind, or the marriage is dissolved, not on mere separation.

q:
Consider the following statements concerning the Uniform Civil Code under the Constitution of India:
(A) Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all persons.
(B) Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens throughout India.
(C) In the Shah Bano case, the Court held that a Muslim husband’s maintenance liability to his divorced wife was limited to the iddat period.
(D) In Danial Latifi v. Union of India, the Court held that a Muslim husband must make a reasonable and fair provision for his divorced wife’s future, extending beyond the iddat period.
(E) In Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India, the Court discussed Article 44 and the relationship between religion and personal law in a secular society.
e: Art. 44 speaks of citizens 'throughout the territory of India' (B), so A is wrong; Shah Bano allowed maintenance beyond iddat under s.125 CrPC (C wrong); Danial Latifi and Sarla Mudgal are correctly described (D, E).

q: In which of the following cases did Chief Justice John Marshall of the United States Supreme Court state that the Constitution was intended to endure for ages to come and therefore had to be adapted to changing circumstances?
e: Marshall C.J. said this in McCulloch v. Maryland (1819).

q:
Consider the following statements concerning the import and export of hazardous waste under the Hazardous Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, 1989:
(A) The import and export of hazardous waste are not permissible under Rule 11.
(B) The import and export of hazardous waste are permissible for recycling and reuse.
(C) An occupier importing or exporting hazardous waste must provide information in Form 5A.
(D) An occupier importing or exporting hazardous waste must comply with the Basel Convention.
(E) The Ministry of Environment and Forests is the nodal ministry for dealing with the transboundary movement of hazardous waste.
e: NTA's key is option C (A, B, D and E). The 1989 Rules bar import for dumping and disposal but allow it for recycling and reuse, subject to the Basel Convention, with the MoEF as nodal ministry.

q:
Arrange the following advisory opinions of the Supreme Court under Article 143(1) of the Constitution in chronological order, from earliest to latest:

(B) In re Special Courts Bill
(C) In re Keshav Singh
(D) In re Berubari Union and Exchange of Enclaves
e: Berubari (1960), Sea Customs Act (1963), Keshav Singh (1964), Special Courts Bill (1978).

q: The constitutive theory of State recognition has been advocated by which of the following jurists?
e: The constitutive theory of recognition is associated with Oppenheim, Anzilotti and Holland; Hall and Brierly are declaratory theorists.

Arrange the following chapters of the Companies Act, 2013, in ascending order according to their chapter numbers:
(A) Share Capital and Debentures
(B) Prospectus and Allotment of Securities

(D) Appointment and Qualification of Directors
e: Companies Act, 2013: Ch. III Prospectus and Allotment, Ch. IV Share Capital and Debentures, Ch. X Audit and Auditors, Ch. XI Appointment and Qualification of Directors.

q: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, held at Stockholm in 1972, incorporated the “Assimilative Capacity Principle” under which of the following principles?
e: Principle 6 of the Stockholm Declaration restricts discharge of pollutants beyond the environment's capacity to render them harmless (assimilative capacity).

q:

(A) Brother
(B) Sister’s son
(C) Son of a predeceased son
(D) Father
e: Son of a predeceased son is Class I; father, brother and sister's son are Class II heirs, in that order of entries.

q:
Arrange the following stages of devolution of property under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, in the correct order for a Hindu male who dies intestate:
(A) First, upon the heirs specified in Class I of the Schedule.
(B) If there are no Class I heirs, upon the heirs specified in Class II of the Schedule.
(C) If there are no agnates, upon the cognates of the deceased.
(D) If there are no Class I or Class II heirs, upon the agnates of the deceased.
e: Section 8 HSA: Class I heirs, then Class II heirs, then agnates, then cognates.

q: Which of the following is not a ground for issuing a writ of prohibition?
o: Violation of the principles of natural justice
An error of law apparent on the face of the record
e: Prohibition lies for excess of jurisdiction, natural-justice violations, infringement of fundamental rights or fraud; an error of law apparent on the face of the record is a ground for certiorari.

q: The Supreme Court held that the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle form part of customary international law and Indian domestic law in which of the following cases?
o: Kinkri Devi v. State of Himachal Pradesh (1987)
Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India (1996)
Vellore Citizens’ Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996)
Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra v. State of Uttar Pradesh (1985)
e: In Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum (1996) the Supreme Court held the precautionary and polluter-pays principles to be part of Indian environmental law.

q:
Which of the following promissory notes would be valid under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881?
(A) “I promise to pay ₹500 seven days after my marriage to C.”
(B) “I promise to pay B or order ₹500.”
(C) “I promise to pay B ₹500, first deducting any money that B may owe me.”
(D) “I acknowledge myself to be indebted to B in the sum of ₹1,000, payable on demand, for value received.”
e: Under s.4 NI Act a note needs an unconditional undertaking. A (contingent) and C (deduction) are invalid, while B and D are valid.
